aramaug said:
Here's the line with emphasis added: "The girl with the me who is me who is Ami I am Ami." I think bold is Narrator Ami and underline is Ami Arakawa. Narrator Ami is inside Ami's head and conflates the two of them because of the infection that is driving them both mad, but they're not the same person. Narrator Ami remembers things like "our youth" together, she wasn't Akira's daughter/niece.
Click to expand...
No that won't make any context sense. Narrator Ami was ranting on how her role was taken by Maya in last sentence. And then she said "The girl with the me who is me who is Ami I am Ami. Can you hear me?". The subject should stay same between two sucessive sentences. Furthermore, the girl is with me instead of within me. I can concede that Narrator Ami is referring the current Maya so that the line would be interpreted as "The Maya with me - Ami in the simulation, who is also me that is Narrator Ami." Though Maya being same narrator is something I also insisted, but that's another topic.

Now. I don't remember Narrator said something along lines of "our youth together". Even if so, I don't see why that would render Narrator Ami not Akira's daughter/niece? They did spend their lives together before and after accident. She claimed to be the girl with broken wings in aforementioned poem which reminds us of another poem from earlier time. Here we learn that girl with broken wings is at least a girl being constantly molested and engaged since childhood. Neither Ami nor Maya we have now is in line with these description. Unless, I mean, you come back to theory that Narrator Ami is real daughter/niece of Akira. At least she knew what happened. If Ami was the fake person wish of Akira generated and attributed all daughter part of Maya to, it must be natural for her to know it all.


However, I do believe that Narrator Ami is connected to current Ami, through Sekai in her head. Remember that Sekai had same poetry talent and title "The girl who can't breathe". Both the Sekai and Narrator Ami addressed their poems to an unknown "boy". I talked once it's suspicious that Sekai and Ami has really no apparent differences to separate. If I have to further expand on it, I have to guess that "Sekai", not the feeble and sentimental woman we've witnessed in Kyoto but that harsh monster constantly haunted and encourged Akira to prey on girls and do incest, might be a production of wish performed by Narrator Ami to help her finish her mission. After all, the family in Recap was perfect for whichever Ami. That's world she wished.



Again we are assuming there are multiple layer of Amis working on different meta-levels but we are always reminded that by Himawari. How much does our current Ami know remains to be seen. But she's clearly for help in the latest Happy Event. Sekai, or her archetype has infected her too deep. Though if Ami was really created to let Akira gain another chance to be a real father. Something must happened to subverse their roles, making Ami an incest machine and Maya an eternal loner. I can't pinpoint the initiative for that. But it's constantly mentioned that world'd always fall apart once Akira starts to love Maya, not sex.

Do you think it's a too bold theory? Since if Sekai was created by Ami, then Pareidolia - User 3 in some most twist way is just same identity as User 4. It can't be, can it? By the way, Sekai died while still pregnant with Ami in Kyoto? Huh? Sekai died in accident because Akira didn't eloped with her to Kyoto before accident. Sekai could survive that way and Ami will be the legal daughter of Akira. Though Nozomu did disappear in their ideal world. The funeral director only mentioned death of Nozomu and Sekai instead of their child. Ami was not a baby when accident occured.

People have reported that Lessons in Love takes from 20 seconds to a whole 3 minutes depending on the system. I'd wager "normal" is under a minute though. Mine takes around 20 seconds, but rarely it just won't open for some reason and I have to start it again.

You can do a couple of things, first of all would be trying to launch it multiple times in a row and see if one of them works. Then you can try running it while shutting down any other programs. Another thing would be to restart your computer to make sure it isn't already running and try it again. To be honest, these are unlikely to work, but you lose nothing trying.
What is likely to work is for you to download the whole thing again, because since other renpy games work, the issue could be something that got corrupted. Just backup your saves, and do not overwrite - but test the new files in a separate location first.

To help with this, you'd have to think about when it stopped working. Was it after changing files? Or was it out of nowhere? The first would suggest an issue with the files getting corrupted, and the second that something changed in your system (which could be fixed by updating drivers and such).

Harem tag explains itself. Incest tag: you have niece and you have an option to have sec with her.

Horror tag: I guess this one is the reason you are asking this question.

The game doesnt have jumpscares, but random flashes. It doesnt meant to scare you but rather happens around when MC sees/hears something he shouldnt.

There are Main Events, Character Events and "Happy Events". First two is your normal harem visual novel with good writing.

Happy Events are where visually and narratively weird. Its is hard to make sense at the start but the more you play the more peices you will have. Those events are rare and far between except at the start of the game. They are not scary but it not gonna make you jerk off either.

These are all common opinions, yes.
1. A weak plot will always work better if you can just move on from it rather than overanalyzing each part. In that sense, it's much easier not to be bothered on so many abandoned supernatural threads when you never had the time to do so, since the natural flow of the game will move past all of them upon reaching chapter 4, and by the time it stops you'll have much more to think about than things like "the three gods that are now four" going nowhere. That's basically the explanation to what I meant by "just don't focus on the supernatural stuff" - we're saying the same thing.

2. Your complaint about character arcs being written worse in chapter 4 is something we've talked about in pretty much every update for the past year. So we're all in overall agreement there as well. Repeated and increasing rate of sexual abuse (Chika/Maya/Tsubasa/Yuki), characters behaving dumbly for the sake of plot (like Niki and Imani), characters behaving in just plain bizarre ways like the whole Sara/Sana thing from Nodokathon 2, the infuriating going nowhere state of Akira for over a year - the list goes on.

And some events are plainly tone-deaf, like almost the entirety of the last dorm wars - and how Rin and Io's event seems completely out of place in that fever dream. Similarly one could say about the entirety of the Christmas update with the gnomes, which was a new level of pathetic.

Conclusion: I just, yeah, a lot has been said already by how chapter 4 is the worst written of them all. The supernatural is not "as bad" as the character arcs, I think I can agree with that. But mainly because the supernatural plot is at a point that it just doesn't matter anymore.

Whatever Selebus says next goes, and it can either retcon everything else, be justified as a "visual representation passed for real", or worse - just don't make sense in retrospect (to a lesser extent with "kyoto", and to a much larger extent with Ami).
"Just enjoy the ride and try to ignore the bad" is the best I can do and suggest tbh.

04 - Sana 1 (Choose Sana)

10 - Futaba 1 (Linked)
11 - Main 4 (Linked)
12 - Main 5 (Linked)
13 - Makoto 2 (Linked)
14 - Tsuneyo 1 (Linked)

**The overall objective is to rebuild Maya, but we also have to trigger the happy event before the end. Basically, we'll get seeds, plant them, craft something with it and exchange it with the girls for body parts. Parallel to that, we have to unlock the happy event via a quiz/craft with Makoto.

1. Check all options at home in order, so that you know where everything is.
2. Go somewhere: (the reset will take you to every location present in a TSS thus far, with their respective girls)
View attachment 5209233

A - (den) get poppy seeds (Noriko).
B - (shack) get lavender seeds (Futaba).
C - (beach) get corpseflower seeds (Sana).
D - (smile) get Maya's torso and start Makoto's quiz (for the happy event).
*there are ten questions about names of gods:
View attachment 5209234

1 - gossamer
2 - giuseppe
3 - pegasus
4 - halftone
5 - floral laura
6 - necalli
7 - onund
8 - harimanti
9 - arramin
10 - apollo
E - (spacy) get rose seeds (Chika).
F - (older) get snapdragon seeds (Yumi).
3. Back at home, plant all the seeds.
4. At home, craft every harvest into something.
5. Go back to every location (with the exception of smile) and trade like this:
A - (den) snapdragon for pelvis.
B - (shack) roses for left arm.
C - (beach) crown for right arm.
D - (spacy) perfume for left leg.
E - (older) opium for right leg.
6. Go back home and craft a stick bouquet.
7. Go back to (smile) and trade the bouquet for a Koi fish.
8. Back at home, search the internet for Koi.
9. Go back to the beach (this triggers the happy event).
10. Back at home, go to the pc and check every message (this is not necessary, but, doing it here, you can read all of them at once if you want).
11. Rebuild Maya.
18 - Main 7 (Linked)
Savefile for 0.52
*Walkthrough mod is needed.
**Green Route means that this is a save in which there is no missed event, aka Akira has done everything he possibly could.
***Every stat (Love/Lust/Headpats) has been bumped to an amount that would get you through any requirements automatically (restricted to the ones that have been unlocked for grinding). All unlockables (outfits) are also unlocked, as are the bonus scenes.
View attachment 5209220 View attachment 5209222 View attachment 5209223
Renpy saves in two separate locations. First one is the easiest. Either go to:

1. locate your game directory (wherever you installed it), the structure should be "lessons in love (or whatever you named it)">"game">"saves". Just drop the file there.

2. Locate your system drive, the structure should be "C: (it's usually C)" > "Users" > "your user name" > "AppData" > "Roaming" > "Renpy" > "Test 2 (this is the name Selebus gave LessonsInLove in the registry)". Drop the file there.

Now, the name of the file dictates in what page it will be. If it's "1-1-LT1", it will be the first page, in the first spot. If it's "9-6-LT1", it will be the 9th page, in the 6th spot.

Notice: There will be no update next month, 0.53 should be coming on November 1st.

spoilers.title: Green Route
spoilers.html:
*Walkthrough mod is needed.
**Green Route means that this is a save in which there is no missed event, aka Akira has done everything he possibly could.
***Every stat (Love/Lust/Headpats) has been bumped to an amount that would get you through any requirements automatically (restricted to the ones that have been unlocked for grinding). All unlockables (outfits) are also unlocked, as are the bonus scenes.
View attachment 5209220 View attachment 5209222 View attachment 5209223
Renpy saves in two separate locations. First one is the easiest. Either go to:

1. locate your game directory (wherever you installed it), the structure should be "lessons in love (or whatever you named it)">"game">"saves". Just drop the file there.

2. Locate your system drive, the structure should be "C: (it's usually C)" > "Users" > "your user name" > "AppData" > "Roaming" > "Renpy" > "Test 2 (this is the name Selebus gave LessonsInLove in the registry)". Drop the file there.

Now, the name of the file dictates in what page it will be. If it's "1-1-LT1", it will be the first page, in the first spot. If it's "9-6-LT1", it will be the 9th page, in the 6th spot.

My guess is that, as usual, Selebus didn't think this through.

On one hand, Himawari seems to imitate what she knows about the person, like with Touka and Sana. Which is why people can tell them apart. I'd highly doubt that if she was actually channeling their own thoughts anyone would be able to tell the difference.

And yet, much earlier when she explains why she doesn't channel Nodoka's mind, or that she dislikes "feeling what her mom feels" by getting her form, implies that she actually channels their minds.

So, which one is it? Because during the reset quiz she clearly channels each person's thoughts, thus we'd have to assume it's actually the channeling that's true. Could she be lying to Akira about it being only his perception? (or Tsubasa's, and Nodoka's?)

Back to Selebus not thinking this through. I don't mean that he didn't think about it because he's dumb, but maybe because he's lazy. And thus he just decided that Himawari can do either. Sometimes she channels people's thoughts, and sometimes she just messes with their perception. Basically, whatever Selebus needs to happen does. As it is with everything else.

My interpretation is that Himawari essentially "loads a character", obtaining both their forms and inventories (aka what characters know and feel, and even speaking patterns), but it's still her behind the keyboard at the end of the day and it's up to her acting/understanding/perception tampering skills to make everything look seamless, or it's up to her to decide whether being a seamless imposter is needed. Though her impersonation does fail some times, I do believe that Himawari does obtain what a character knows when she become them. Examples of Sana and Ayane are subtle, but a more noticeable example would be the entire reset5. Himawari being the fact checker for multiple girls is only made possible by becoming them. This is more apparent when Himawari initially refuses to be Ayane, saying that "Just read those (cards) and go without a fact checker".

For Yumi and Tsuneyo, one could say those knowledge could simply be obtained by being a good trans-dimensional spectator, including Yumi secretly masturbating to Sensei. However, that shouldn't be the case of Maya Prime. When being Maya Prime, Himawari is quite clearly overwhelmed by whatever is going on in Maya's head, implying that at that moment, Himawari does have access to what Maya Prime's been through; memories and experiences alike.

I mean, obviously at this point it's whatever Selebus decides to retcon, but if we go back to the explanation of what the wishing well is, it's more likely that it connects you to a reality where what you want is true, rather than actually creating something out of nowhere.

I arrive at two theories from this, one is easier to be correct, the other is rather interesting, but less likely to be what Selebus intended.

1. It's that the Wishing Well sends the one that jumps down through it into another reality. This has been commented many times over these past few months, since the reset that showed us different realities (possible). In that sense, everything is real. Nothing is reset ever, there are countless broken worlds left behind from each time the world "reset", which actually means transporting to another reality. And in that same sense, everything is fake and already over. In fact, most of things the characters have ever experienced now lie in abandoned worlds.

2. This one is quite interesting to me, but less likely. NAO could be referencing the fact that what Akira is experiencing is a literal library. In the sense that the game takes place after everything has already happened. That's why she knows that nothing will make a difference, because all has already happened.

This finds help in the fact that Himawari exists, and yet there are counterpoints to this - like Himawari intending to change things. Unless she means to change things in her/NAO's present in the far future, to change things in Akira's present would either mean it's still the present, or simply that she indeed can change the past.
Maybe this is all excessive deepthinking.

posts.content_html_raw:
Hey, can I say something I've been waiting to say for ages? Sorry if being too sassy. Sometimes I just can't put with him.





It's generally refreshing to see someone finally took upon himself to teach Akira a good lesson. He knew it all along. He remembered how Nozumu completely dominated him and it hurt him more than grooming of Sekai. He believed that Sekai saved him and became his guardian angel. It's really interesting that in young Akira's mind his brother and sister-in-law were God and angel.
Oh, and then Nozumu beated and abused Sekai too. He probably sodomized child Akira from some of the inkling we have. So that's twice a good job. So Nozumu was kind of a karma enforcer to each Arakawa. And he's completely a good father to Ami who unfortunately never learned to appreciate any amount of normalcy due to her mother. Damn our badass bro Nozumu never did anything wrong.



I knew you could say that it's an afterthought and it's the very abuse caused by Nozumu led Akira to the rabbit hole as of today. But you know what, I'm not an adherent of Post hoc ergo propter hoc fallacy. His cowardliness and escapism were something he chose from the beginning and all the conflicts with Sekai and Nozumu only made him easier to drown in self-pity. With that in mind, he'd eventually become the one he is today regardless of the past. I'm not saying that what Nozumu did was a good thing now that Akira became a truly monster somehow cherished by all. It's just a really sardonic prospect to piece things together considering what Akira became was nothing more than of a copycat between these two. He never managed to overcome any of them.

It's even more ironic if you think about what happened afterwards. Noriko had sex with him out of sheer pity regardless of what she claimed, and that's all. Pathetic. He could never get rid of him. He even never learned to enjoy the sensation of being powerful in regard to little ones. I guess you can't escape your past even if living inside a dream.

This is not an endorsement for him to become a criminal obviously, but I don't think that assuming it would be simple for him to carve a regular life for himself is accurate either.

If you'd say "I wish that at the end of this story, Akira suffers for what he did - because having a trauma is not a free-pass to do similar things to other people" I think a lot of people would agree with that in general. It's just that his karma cannot be the violence done to him in the beginning of it all because it doesn't make chronological sense. I'll skip your depiction of Nozomu because that's just weird, and my opinion on it can be assumed from what I said. Ami saying that she thought he was a regular father also shouldn't mean much, given that she was both a child (very limited information) and could just be lying as well.
One point I would like to address that you didn't is that Niki, and especially her parents are guilty in all of this. Obviously I'm limited by how good of a writer Selebus will be here, but in a real life situation, and what he decided to write in that event, Niki and her family suspected for years what was going on and did nothing. They weren't sort of acquainted, he was her boyfriend and before that he was in her house everyday. Again, it's a writing issue more than anything, but any sane person would have investigated the situation further or called social services.

What I got from that event is that Akira never had a likely chance to recover from the start (just from how overwhelming everything was), which explains a lot of his passive attitude (and also makes me much less interested in him as a protagonist, since I think he ought to just go to a mental institution), and that a HUGE part of why Niki will never leave him is guilt.
One final point is that the information we have about the whole situation is also rather fragmented, and at times contradictory. Why would Sekai choose to stay with Nozomu after what she saw? Where were Saki and Yuu? Was Nozomu Akira's guardian? I'm not really satisfied with the current known information and thus generally refrain from looking too much into it for now.

That certainly puts things into perspective, and the language barrier is definitely a factor. For myself, I don't think you need to go so far as to apologize, or delete anything - although the explanation/apology is appreciated and corrects any possible misunderstanding we might have had. I'll be going on a ramble about the themes of LiL now:
I have already said this a couple of times, but I think it merits saying again that the public LiL draws is a heavily charged one. Although not all, a lot of us have gone through something in our own pasts. So it can very easily veer into an emotional and delicate place.

Once I got into a light argument with DeSkel over people being able to overcome tragedies or not. And I think, especially for someone that has gone through some tough shit, we tend to try our hardest to convince ourselves that we can both overcome and become better despite what was done to us. I think that's the right mindset to have. But I also have to reluctantly concede, especially as I grow older, that some things just break and there's no putting them back together. But that's a personal thing, I certainly have no intention of enforcing my opinion in anyway.

I only say this because what I got from your story was that you felt some sort of "see? I did my best to become a better person despite what was done to me. You didn't, Akira. You deserve to suffer for losing yourself in it". I don't know you enough to say it was this exactly, nor is it my intent to try to guess or get to know you more. I'm just trying to say that we have no issue with that. For instance, I have a thing with revenge. When I see a character being mistreated in a fictional story, I'll rage and want death on their abusers for the smallest things. That's also fine, because it's all fiction and I'm not like this in real life.

At the end of the day, we're talking about fiction. Not many know this about me, but I receive about 10-20 messages daily hating me personally about my opinions on fictional stories. I like to think this was not our intent here, however you react to LiL or anything else is your deal. Mostly we were confused because your argument didn't make sense logically. It was not that you couldn't want Akira to suffer for the shit he's done (that's totally your prerrogative), but that him being punished preemptively for the very things he'd do, because of said "punishment", doesn't fit. But I think this discussion is settled.

posts.content_html_raw:
SageBestGirl said:
And regarding this comment from Himawari about the smell on Alt Maya Prime's scarf, what's your interpretation regarding this comment?
Click to expand...
1 - Maya Prime is the one we meet at the beginning of the game, and that is "slipped" at the end of chapter 3. She's moved to the "Replica of Heaven" (Noriko's TSS), under the care of AmIOkay.

2 - New Maya is the "reset" version of Maya that shows up at chapter 4, most recently having been beheaded by Ami.

3 - Alternate Maya Prime (or just alternate maya) is the Maya that Ayane meets during the "cycles hopping reset". She's the one that discloses the nature of her notes, and that gives Ayane the original version of the green scarf. That same scarf is later recovered by Himawari during last christmas.

4 - Shadow Maya is a ghost Maya that only appears during "Frankincense", behing Akira at the church. No new information since then, but it could point out to a narrator Maya.

5 - Narrator Maya is an old theory that states that one of the mysterious narrators is Maya, alongside Himawari and possibly others.

6 - Original Maya refers to the Maya before any of the resets, possibly the one we see during the happy event when she's talking to Akira on the roof of a different school.

7 - AmIOkay, YouDidIt, Moyo and the nameless Mayas are entities that resemble Maya physically, but aren't confirmed to be her as of right now.

8 - Ami suggests Maya is a doll, and there is a current theory that Maya could be a version of Ami and vice-versa.
There are two main theories as of its release and until now:

1. The nostalgic scent could simply refer to Ayane's scent, since she had been wearing it for a while - and Ayane's Hima-chan's mom.

2. The nostalgic scent could refer to Maya, although we don't know which one. Do mind that a possible connection between Himawari and Maya had been established in chapter 3, when the narrator alludes to the fact that she learned a lesson from someone (very close to Akira) about taking their own safety for granted, foreshadowing Maya's demise at the end of chapter 3.

This assumes Maya Primes survives the ordeal (which has been more or less confirmed), and that she talks to Himawari about it at some point. Things could also be simpler, mainly referring to the fact that Himawari was the one that had the green scarf be delivered to Maya Prime during the events of this cycle.

3. Other possibilities include the scent being from a different timeline (possibly Himawari's), a specific Maya, or even Akira's rented studio.
I think we're likely to find out what the nostalgic scent refers to during the next update, or at least narrow down the possibilities as we learn more about Himawari's origins.

What are the signs that Maya Prime will return at the end of chapter 4? Could you share them with me please?
Click to expand...
It's a few perspectives that have convinced me of it. Game directorally-wise, I think it would be a huge shame if Maya's purity route was used to explain their backstory and the full scene we saw that one frame of loli maya on top of Sensei. The idea of rescuing prime during the dark route is kinda nice ngl, but it would be at the cost of making her purity route all flashback no "focus on me now, we finally have time to relax and enjoy each other", and she's been robbed of that all game. I want her purity route to let her enjoy being herself again (like returning to the festival, then spending the next day entirely inside his home just being together).

If she had a major set of updates after her return but before dark route you could fit that kind of backstory pretty seamlessly. Our current Maya is quite a way off from being prime and her last update showed Sel is ready to start drip feeding her return. A while ago I calculated how much longer we'd have left before a theoretical chapter 6 dark route which I counted it as 4 resets, two resets for an extra chapter's extension to chapter 4 which Sel said was going to be the longest by far (and which would make the name infinite spring actually meaningful) and then a chapter 5 which would theoretically get us back to a more regular feeling LIL with a Akira who has hopefully stopped being a doormat by this point. That kind of time extension would give Maya enough time to get more sentience points if Sel keeps doing it, and then has chapter 5 to talk about that backstory (You could even throw in a bit more shorter term tragedy here. There's a reason I wanted Maya to have invite events and lust grinding before Prime came back)

Ingame evidence, most I could point to is Chapter 3 starting with the idea of losing Maya and ending with actually losing Maya, and the gods threatening to punish him for not taking something that doesn't belong to him, and then punishing him with it by taking Maya. There's a history of these threads being given early, and being followed through on by the end. The gods have instructed him to rape someone, and even after taking Maya away they still want him to do it (Pareidolia still wants to work together in the narration when chapter 4 begins) and they demonstrate they still want him to rape someone when they offer to give Prime back if he rapes Karin, which he refuses to do at the time. If this thread is to be followed through he needs to rape someone who wouldn't be willing in any way, and I've previously discussed who I think the only target left could be. Since then Nao has started to say she thinks Akira's hot so it might be impossible to rape her now which just leans into that harder.

spoilers.title: Noriko text
spoilers.html:
vpa "Noriko Nakayama — please report to the principal’s office. "
n "Report to the-"
n "This..."
n "This has gotta be a dream, right?"
vpa "It is not a dream."
scene molerat31
with dissolve
n "Like {i}fuck{/i} it’s not a dream, disembodied PA voice! I’ve never heard a school announcement {i}respond{/i} before! And this isn’t even my school!"
vpa "This is everyone’s school."
scene molerat32
with dissolve
vpa "The time is currently 7:31 PM. Today’s forecast is partly cloudy with a chance of nightfall. "
vpa "You are happy here. There is no reason for you to leave."
n "Okay, sure. But why am I holding an egg?"
vpa "Reasons. "
scene molerat33
with dissolve
n "Alright. I’ve seriously gotta lay off the melatonin before bed. I’ve heard of it causing nightmares, but this is just flat out weird."
n "One second I’m shopping with Ami and Nee-chan, the next I have to bring an egg to the principal at 7:31 PM. That makes total sense."
play sound "pabell.mp3"
$ renpy.pause(2, hard=True)
m "Noriko Nakayama — your attendance is required for the Transpacific Sadness Symposium in nine minutes."

with dissolve2
n "Maya?..."
n "Transpacific...Sadness Symposium?..."
m "Your guide is waiting just beyond the door. Please dry off your shoes and follow her to the best of your ability — but be warned."
m "She skitters like a crab. And for every leg that snaps at the joint, a piece of you will be removed. "
n "Like...my clothes? Because I’ve had some weird sex dreams before, but nothing even close to this."
m "This is not a dream."

spoilers.title: Sana text
spoilers.html:
vpa "Sana Sakakibara — your attendance is required for the Transpacific Sadness Symposium in four days."
vpa "The current temperature is sixty-five degrees Fahrenheit. The time of day is to be determined shortly."
vpa "Until then, feel free to make yourself comfortable somewhere between darkness and daytime. Refreshments will be provided momentarily."
sa "...what?"
play sound "pabell.mp3"
$ renpy.pause(4, hard=True)
play music "ichiyarakka2.mp3"
vpa "In order to replicate the critical success of “Ad Infinitum,” a familiar song will now play on repeat through the loudspeaker. Though it may not be familiar to you."
vpa "Please take a seat on the bench and wait patiently for your number to be called. Your guide will be arriving shortly."
play sound "static.mp3"
scene knifeboy19 with flash
stop sound
"She could not believe her eyes or her ears or her mouth. This was insanity. This was crazy. This was super fucking weird. It was chaos. Madness. Other negative adjectives!"
"There was no wind, just the faint smell of chlorine as music bounced off of expertly painted walls (or wall?) of a dome that held her like the unmoving nucleus of a cruel joke."
"Right now, she was the unborn child of reality itself, wriggling and {i}thinking{/i} on the floor of Earth’s uterus. She did not know what was approaching for the silence had already settled in."
sa "I’m going fucking insane."
"She wasn’t. This was REAL. Super real! That’s why other people kept experiencing it! But she didn’t know that yet. She doesn’t know anything yet because she isn’t ALLOWED TO. She is SUPPRESSED."
"Reach forward! Touch the walls! Feel that wet lead paint on your fingertips before bringing to your lips and painting them blue only for your skin to follow suit! Skin suit! Special Ami! She is here!"

spoilers.html:
vpa "Good morning, Yumi Yamaguchi. The time is currently 8:47 AM. Today’s weather forecast calls for highs of 78 degrees Fahrenheit and lows of 65."

vpa "And remember — there is no {i}you{/i} in Yumi. But there is Yumi in you."

posts.content_html_raw:
With another 3 weeks before the next release, I'd love to get other peoples' take on a few of the bigger pieces of lore before the story continues. If you've already posted on these topics in the last few months, and don't have anything new to say, its okay, but if you have new thoughts or predictions, let 'em rip:

1.
The Wishing Well - what was the nature of the wish, who made it, were there multiple wishes?

Kaoridolia, but there might be some Sekaiori in here too(?):
k "There are many ways in which one can become a god, but the part that {i}really{/i} matters is being able to provide something for someone. "
k "Look at cats and dogs and other domesticated animals. To them, humans are akin to God. They provide food, shelter, the whole shabang. And that’s what {i}we{/i} do for {i}you.{/i} "
k "Well...maybe not food and shelter. You guys have gotten pretty good at figuring that part out. But we give you something to believe in. And with how curious your species is, that probably means...something?"
k "I don’t know, man. There’s a reason we’re dying out, though. And it’s because you guys keep asking questions about how it’s even {i}possible{/i} for us to be alive when all logic states we shouldn’t."
k "That shit’s annoying as hell though because most of us are {i}created{/i} by you guys. So, like...why even bother making a god at all when you’re just going to abandon it?"
k "We can’t ever {i}die{/i} until we’re truly forgotten, so most of us just have to fucking pace back and forth forever and ever, twiddling our thumbs while waiting for that to happen."
k "Others take the opposite path, though. Others want to become stronger. So they reach out and touch you any way they can. Sometimes literally, sometimes not."
k "The ones who reach the top of the ladder are the ones who make the rules. And the punishment we receive for breaking them is even worse a fate than death."
k "They turn us into {i}you.{/i}"

k "Humans...animals...plants...{i}anything{/i} could have been a god at some point. And anything can turn back {i}into{/i} a god once someone believes it."
k "It doesn’t need to be a group of people who believe it either. And it doesn’t need to be approved. It just needs to be thought — because we {i}do{/i} defy logic. But that makes all of us equal."
k "No one of us can be more {i}real{/i} than the others because it’s all just make believe. And, to some people, that makes all of this seem silly. Which is where those promises come in. "
k "But even {i}those{/i} are only as real as you make them out to be. "
k "Which turns the whole spirituality thing into a game of choosing which benefits sound the coolest or whatever it is that will help you cope with the fact that you {i}will{/i} die one day. You’re mortal."

k "But what happens if you start to think of {i}yourself{/i} as God? Can you make yourself immortal by just willing it into existence?"
k "Do you think that’s what {i}you’ve{/i} done? Do you think that explains where you’ve found yourself and why you can’t escape? Is it you? Or someone else? Who is it? Why? What do they see in you?"
k "There’s a place at the bottom of the Wishing Well where forgotten gods can rest. That’s where I was until you came along and pulled me up. But how did you find me there? And who forgot me in the first place?"
k "I could tell you I know the answer, sure. But I’d be lying. Just like I’ve lied about so many other things. Just like I’m {i}still{/i} lying, but that’s just what we do. "
k "It isn’t just humans who are searching for life and death while attempting to make sense of everything in between. It’s {i}everyone.{/i}"
k "You are our gods. We are yours. These are the gears that power the machine — this is the bucket that pulls water from the well."
k "But one day, that well will dry up."

2.
Cottontails/Gods - which characters are partially divine or totally divine? Sod in the Seedbed introduced the term, and besides outright telling us Tsuneyo is one, hinted that "And there are several others you may also be familiar with." Sensei has to be at least the male version if not outright deific, right? The world literally revolves around him.

I feel like there's an argument to be made for all of the single-parent girls to be at least a Cottontail. Hell, maybe everyone in the dorms/class?

"rabbit" or "rabbit hole" appear 120 different times in the text. Sel's a reptile guy so it's not just a turn of phrase he likes, especially with the cottontail thing. Is rabbit hole synonymous with the wishing well, and does it all tie in to the cottontails? They are the ones that can be ridden by gods. They are the ones that can learn to slip? But those who learn to slip actually go to another world, where we're told Sensei is different and sort of just projects his consciousness there.

Or am I just getting sucked into Selebus' schizophrenia, and it's all just a bunch of word salad?


Sod In The Seedbed:
"Tsuneyo Tojo is something that we in the office call a “cottontail.” But no, not like the rabbit (despite how greatly you may wish to repeatedly breed her at this point in time)."
"We call them cottontails strictly because girls like her are exceptional when it comes to avoiding predation, but somewhat lack in terms of mental capacity, often mistaking {i}what{/i} to avoid."
"Such girls are born when a greater power mates with a lesser one. And there are several others you may also be familiar with."
"To anyone else, I’m sure they look like normal girls. But to me, a person experienced in dealing with them, they’re anything but. In fact, they’re really special."
"We can bottle their blood to cure cancer, but have been told we’re not allowed to do that since it messes with the circle of life. "
"Additionally, they excrete a special fluid from the glands inside of their vaginae that makes sexual intercourse marginally more enjoyable for male partners. "
"The last and most important factoid in regard to what makes the cottontail special is their relation to the seedbed. But you already know what that is-"
"Wait, you don’t?"
"Hm. Okay. That makes things a little more difficult. But I’ll try to break it down for you in the easiest way possible. "
"Each one of us has a number. Think of it like a rating that determines how closely related we are to “God.” So you can think of the seedbed as like...an airport lounge! "
"It’s a lounge that only people with certain ratings can reach, and the cottontails are among that ilk. "
"Unfortunately, due to the nature of their existence, most of them are completely unaware that such lounges exist, electing to live out peaceful lives in fictional Japanese cities instead."
"So yeah! Basically, she’s special. "
"{b}BUT SHE WILL NEVER KNOW HOW SPECIAL SHE IS UNLESS YOU FORCE-FEED HER THE INFORMATION REQUIRED TO PROGRESS BEYOND THE-{/b}"

Flora:
"A girl with special eyes — the kind that remind you of an unnamed celestial body taking cover behind several tree canopies, distributing its light among the leaves and feeding them the correct brand of radiation."
"In the daylight, where the majority of these bodies can not be seen or witnessed, is when it’s safest to lurk through the foliage the way I’m doing now."
"But in springtime, some of that safety begins to dissipate."
"You see, this is when nature is the hungriest. Because the everblooming nature of nature’s nature isn’t all that natural when you really think about it."
"The colors makes the other colors hungry."
"Or jealous."
"And that envy propels them to feast on more of those unknown celestial eyes or light or whatever it was to increase their colors and make their patterns more distinct."
"If you can’t identify which flowers you shan’t eat, it makes it easier for those flowers to eat you. And consuming the blood of a human just accelerates that floral desire to out-flora the florum."
"EDITOR’S NOTE: Florum /ˈflôrəm/ ~ Multiple types of flora combining to create one universal floral entity [[EX: lesser god/cottontail]. "
"But anyway, yeah. That’s what those special eyes remind me of."
"They remind me of a lot of other things as well. But that’s exactly why I’m so unsettled by the existence of the non-floral entity I’m searching for. "
"If it joins the florum, cutting it down won’t be as easy as slipping on a pair of gardening gloves and propagating some pieces to replant in a tiny ceramic pot."
"I’ll have to crush its head like you would a snake- for severing it would be too painful and freezing it would be too slow. And I can’t fit one more girl in my freezer or there will be no space for Barbara’s favorite movie."

3.
The Xoanon - Is Nao-chan an aspect of the Xoanon? Is Sensei an aspect of the Xoanon? Is one or more of the Ami's we've an aspect of the Xoanon? The one keeping the closest eye on Sensei is probably Ami, right? Nao has "sat there and watched" quite a bit at this point (Kittens), but she's actively done things to others too (Den of the Mole Rat) so she's not just a passive observer.

x "I am the cataloger of what you’ve felt and what you’ll feel. "
x "I am the one who dissects the impact your “actions” will have on the immediate story — then decides whether or not adjustments should be made and informs the ones concerned."
x "I have watched it all."
x "I have gotten drunk off of your pain and reveled in your joy in those few fleeting moments where it occurred."
x "You may call me a guardian angel if you like, but I prefer the name “Nao.”"
s "You’re no guardian. A guardian {i}protects{/i} people from pain — they don’t just sit there and watch."
x "They do when they know it all serves a greater purpose."
x "We all have a role to play. We’re all cogs in a much bigger machine. You needn’t be jealous because I’m a bigger, shinier cog than you."

k "There are many ways in which one can become a god, but the part that {i}really{/i} matters is being able to provide something for someone. "
k "Look at cats and dogs and other domesticated animals. To them, humans are akin to God. They provide food, shelter, the whole shabang. And that’s what {i}we{/i} do for {i}you.{/i} "
k "Well...maybe not food and shelter. You guys have gotten pretty good at figuring that part out. But we give you something to believe in. And with how curious your species is, that probably means...something?"
k "I don’t know, man. There’s a reason we’re dying out, though. And it’s because you guys keep asking questions about how it’s even {i}possible{/i} for us to be alive when all logic states we shouldn’t."
k "That shit’s annoying as hell though because most of us are {i}created{/i} by you guys. So, like...why even bother making a god at all when you’re just going to abandon it?"
k "We can’t ever {i}die{/i} until we’re truly forgotten, so most of us just have to fucking pace back and forth forever and ever, twiddling our thumbs while waiting for that to happen."
k "Others take the opposite path, though. Others want to become stronger. So they reach out and touch you any way they can. Sometimes literally, sometimes not."
k "The ones who reach the top of the ladder are the ones who make the rules. And the punishment we receive for breaking them is even worse a fate than death."
k "They turn us into {i}you.{/i}"

k "Humans...animals...plants...{i}anything{/i} could have been a god at some point. And anything can turn back {i}into{/i} a god once someone believes it."
k "It doesn’t need to be a group of people who believe it either. And it doesn’t need to be approved. It just needs to be thought — because we {i}do{/i} defy logic. But that makes all of us equal."
k "No one of us can be more {i}real{/i} than the others because it’s all just make believe. And, to some people, that makes all of this seem silly. Which is where those promises come in. "
k "But even {i}those{/i} are only as real as you make them out to be. "
k "Which turns the whole spirituality thing into a game of choosing which benefits sound the coolest or whatever it is that will help you cope with the fact that you {i}will{/i} die one day. You’re mortal."

k "But what happens if you start to think of {i}yourself{/i} as God? Can you make yourself immortal by just willing it into existence?"
k "Do you think that’s what {i}you’ve{/i} done? Do you think that explains where you’ve found yourself and why you can’t escape? Is it you? Or someone else? Who is it? Why? What do they see in you?"
k "There’s a place at the bottom of the Wishing Well where forgotten gods can rest. That’s where I was until you came along and pulled me up. But how did you find me there? And who forgot me in the first place?"
k "I could tell you I know the answer, sure. But I’d be lying. Just like I’ve lied about so many other things. Just like I’m {i}still{/i} lying, but that’s just what we do. "
k "It isn’t just humans who are searching for life and death while attempting to make sense of everything in between. It’s {i}everyone.{/i}"
k "You are our gods. We are yours. These are the gears that power the machine — this is the bucket that pulls water from the well."
k "But one day, that well will dry up."

spoilers.html:
Cottontails/Gods - which characters are partially divine or totally divine? Sod in the Seedbed introduced the term, and besides outright telling us Tsuneyo is one, hinted that "And there are several others you may also be familiar with." Sensei has to be at least the male version if not outright deific, right? The world literally revolves around him.

I feel like there's an argument to be made for all of the single-parent girls to be at least a Cottontail. Hell, maybe everyone in the dorms/class?

"rabbit" or "rabbit hole" appear 120 different times in the text. Sel's a reptile guy so it's not just a turn of phrase he likes, especially with the cottontail thing. Is rabbit hole synonymous with the wishing well, and does it all tie in to the cottontails? They are the ones that can be ridden by gods. They are the ones that can learn to slip? But those who learn to slip actually go to another world, where we're told Sensei is different and sort of just projects his consciousness there.

Or am I just getting sucked into Selebus' schizophrenia, and it's all just a bunch of word salad?


Sod In The Seedbed:
"Tsuneyo Tojo is something that we in the office call a “cottontail.” But no, not like the rabbit (despite how greatly you may wish to repeatedly breed her at this point in time)."
"We call them cottontails strictly because girls like her are exceptional when it comes to avoiding predation, but somewhat lack in terms of mental capacity, often mistaking {i}what{/i} to avoid."
"Such girls are born when a greater power mates with a lesser one. And there are several others you may also be familiar with."
"To anyone else, I’m sure they look like normal girls. But to me, a person experienced in dealing with them, they’re anything but. In fact, they’re really special."
"We can bottle their blood to cure cancer, but have been told we’re not allowed to do that since it messes with the circle of life. "
"Additionally, they excrete a special fluid from the glands inside of their vaginae that makes sexual intercourse marginally more enjoyable for male partners. "
"The last and most important factoid in regard to what makes the cottontail special is their relation to the seedbed. But you already know what that is-"
"Wait, you don’t?"
"Hm. Okay. That makes things a little more difficult. But I’ll try to break it down for you in the easiest way possible. "
"Each one of us has a number. Think of it like a rating that determines how closely related we are to “God.” So you can think of the seedbed as like...an airport lounge! "
"It’s a lounge that only people with certain ratings can reach, and the cottontails are among that ilk. "
"Unfortunately, due to the nature of their existence, most of them are completely unaware that such lounges exist, electing to live out peaceful lives in fictional Japanese cities instead."
"So yeah! Basically, she’s special. "
"{b}BUT SHE WILL NEVER KNOW HOW SPECIAL SHE IS UNLESS YOU FORCE-FEED HER THE INFORMATION REQUIRED TO PROGRESS BEYOND THE-{/b}"

Flora:
"A girl with special eyes — the kind that remind you of an unnamed celestial body taking cover behind several tree canopies, distributing its light among the leaves and feeding them the correct brand of radiation."
"In the daylight, where the majority of these bodies can not be seen or witnessed, is when it’s safest to lurk through the foliage the way I’m doing now."
"But in springtime, some of that safety begins to dissipate."
"You see, this is when nature is the hungriest. Because the everblooming nature of nature’s nature isn’t all that natural when you really think about it."
"The colors makes the other colors hungry."
"Or jealous."
"And that envy propels them to feast on more of those unknown celestial eyes or light or whatever it was to increase their colors and make their patterns more distinct."
"If you can’t identify which flowers you shan’t eat, it makes it easier for those flowers to eat you. And consuming the blood of a human just accelerates that floral desire to out-flora the florum."
"EDITOR’S NOTE: Florum /ˈflôrəm/ ~ Multiple types of flora combining to create one universal floral entity [[EX: lesser god/cottontail]. "
"But anyway, yeah. That’s what those special eyes remind me of."
"They remind me of a lot of other things as well. But that’s exactly why I’m so unsettled by the existence of the non-floral entity I’m searching for. "
"If it joins the florum, cutting it down won’t be as easy as slipping on a pair of gardening gloves and propagating some pieces to replant in a tiny ceramic pot."
"I’ll have to crush its head like you would a snake- for severing it would be too painful and freezing it would be too slow. And I can’t fit one more girl in my freezer or there will be no space for Barbara’s favorite movie."

Still new here, just completed 2nd playthrough, but wanted to share some thoughts on Io/Akira and Akira/Sekai parallels. Apologies if this has been discussed before:

First playthrough, Stomachache skip all the way. It felt too evil and gross. All of the loving dialogue and scenes post-skip with Io initially seemed to confirm it as the right choice.

However, after the 2nd playthrough doing the opposite and green routing it, my feeling changed.

If we skip, at one point Io asks if Akira is an Angel, and now she sees him as one and only savior.

I think this is a direct parallel to how Akira saw Sekai. When she opened the closet door and he saw her, she was his Angel. When things became groomy, the feelings of her saving him conflated with the obvious no-no of grooming/stat-rape/etc. Part of the reason Akria is so fucked up is that his feelings for Sekai are all so jumbled with pure good and bad. He can intellectually understand that what she did was wrong, as shown by his current self hate for repeating it, but he cannot conform that thought with her being his savior.

I think that if we skip stomachache, we become Io's Sekai. She's already messed up from her awful childhood, so the long-term effects can only be pronounced further. Niki talks about this after she catches Akria and Noriko. Sometimes the real damage isnt seen till way down the line.

I think it would really screw with Akira in future events too, since his self-hate has him literally asking for punishment or reprisal at various points. Having Io put him way up on the pedestal will only ensure a greater fall at some point in the future, likely in the dark path section.

posts.content_html_raw:
ArtoriAss1337 said:
recommendations for similar games with some part of same quality at least in storytelling?
Click to expand...
Closest would be "Out of Touch". "Dissonance" is the least bad among the LiL lookalikes, but I personally don't recommend it - just letting you know it exists, alongside "Lost in You".

Stepping a bit away from LiL, if you want the school mystery thing, "Crimson High" is fine, but not that good either. If you simply want something with a story, no matter what it is, then there's "The Fiery Scion" and "Secret Island", those two are heavily D&D based. "Cosy Cafe" is a very soft submissive harem school one. All of these are ongoing games however.

Going into completed games: "Always Fan" and "Parental Love" are plots without supernatural elements. "Now and Then", "City of Broken Dreamers" and "Mist" step more into the fictional aspect of the universe, be it supernatural or technological. "Long live the Princess" is D&D like.

"Last Sovereign" is just amazing (expansive detailed universe, 100+ gameplay, great comedy, decisions affecting a lot), Sierra is a great author of other games as well. However it is rpgm-based, unlike everything mentioned before, and I recommend using a guide for playing it. Lastly, I just think "Boat" is incredible, but that's because I'm a big fan of time-loops and multiple endings. And while it is an amazing game, it is also not for everyone (best definition is "a meme that grew into something serious").

There are tons of games in my recommendation list (on my signature), you can check it out if you want as well (total is almost at 300 games).

posts.content_html_raw:
john doeer said:
wanted to share some thoughts on Io/Akira and Akira/Sekai parallels. [...] Having Io put him way up on the pedestal will only ensure a greater fall at some point in the future, likely in the dark path section.
Click to expand...
This hasn't been discussed before because by the time we got to the "Redeemer Sekai" revelation, we had discussed "stomachache" to death. So I found your point quite interesting to read.
That being said, while the parallel certainly holds water, I think there are some major differences here. First is that Io is much older than Akira was, and he's not directly related to her trauma. What happened to Akira is what we call complex post-traumatic stress disorder (among many other tragedies). In regular PTSD you have a traumatic event that shatters one's mind through overbearing stress, the mind breaks and you have to deal with the consequences of a single event. Both Io and Akira's situations are complex PTSDs, because it's not from one single event, but rather a long continuation of trauma.

The main point here is that Io's trauma, complex or not, ended when she was rescued by her aunt. Her aunt never looked to her in a sexual way, and she was genuinely given a safe place, along with professional help - from then on she had to deal with the consequences of the trauma. In Akira's case, his "rescuer" not only did not separate him from the source of his trauma, but further enhanced said trauma - through years on end. Akira kept being traumatized until Sekai died, pretty much. Io was given the chance, by her Aunt's example, to understand and feel that what her parents did was fucked up. Akira never was, resulting in what you said: he has trouble discerning the most basic feeling that Sekai was a monster.

This is pointed out multiple times, but I think most relevant to this discussion in "stomachache" itself. Io calls him out on it. This is what I mean, Io is a teenager, Akira is an adult. The fact that she is able to call him out on it is that she was far more fortunate than him (in this specific aspect of their conditions) by being actually rescued.

Continuing with this idea, there is also a second difference between these situations, in that Io is aware that Akira is having sex with everyone else. While, certainly, if at one point the dude that "refused to treat her like a doll" suddenly raped her, it would be traumatic, but to what extent exactly? To what extent woult it even be rape at that point? Would Io really be unwilling to let herself be used by this dude in a moment of weakness? Would she not consider it fair game for someone that gave her "so much"? While this ultimately falls to Selebus, I have difficulty seeing Io being utterly broken by Akira having sex with her after telling her that he's fine with not doing it.

In the green path, Io has sex with him, and while it wasn't enjoyable to either of them, they're just fine. I do agree that it is safer for everyone involved because there's no possible downfall waiting to happen, it already has and they crossed it together. At the same time, even if Io venerates her "boyfriend" for being content in "only" having sex with everyone else but her, I don't see how she'd mind that much to take one for the team eventually either. It'd be uncomfortable, obviously, but a mindbreaking tragedy? I'm not convinced.

complex
post-traumatic stress disorder (among many other tragedies). In regular PTSD you have a traumatic event that shatters one's mind through overbearing stress, the mind breaks and you have to deal with the consequences of a single event. Both Io and Akira's situations are
complex
PTSDs, because it's not from one single event, but rather a long continuation of trauma.
The main point here is that Io's trauma, complex or not, ended when she was rescued by her aunt. Her aunt never looked to her in a sexual way, and she was genuinely given a safe place, along with professional help - from then on she had to deal with the
consequences
of the trauma. In Akira's case, his "rescuer" not only did not separate him from the source of his trauma, but further enhanced said trauma - through years on end. Akira kept being traumatized until Sekai died, pretty much. Io was given the chance, by her Aunt's example, to understand and feel that what her parents did was fucked up. Akira never was, resulting in what you said: he has trouble discerning the most basic feeling that Sekai was a monster.
This is pointed out multiple times, but I think most relevant to this discussion in "stomachache" itself. Io calls him out on it. This is what I mean, Io is a teenager, Akira is an adult. The fact that she is able to call him out on it is that she was far more fortunate than him (in this specific aspect of their conditions) by being
actually
rescued.
Continuing with this idea, there is also a second difference between these situations, in that Io is aware that Akira is having sex with everyone else. posts.content_html_raw:
Last month I said I would write something about the death of Tsuneyo's father. Better late than never, I guess?
We've known pretty much since the start of the game that Tsuneyo's father was going to die at some point - it's been repeatedly teased as a possibility. Here's one very explicit example from last Halloween:

0.52 contained strong evidence that he is in fact dead. It starts with the notice of death that is surrounded by USER2's trademark /////.
That image is shown directly after one which has two messages in the styles of USER1 and USER3, respectively.
Possibly the notice of death is meant to explain why there isn't also a message from USER2. In any case, it's connected to him in some way.

Then in "Denoument" some things are said by "Kaori" that heavily imply Mr. Tojo isn't around anymore. First she calls Tsuneyo "tenchou", which translates to manager. Previously, it was her dad that was called Tenchou-sama. The implication is she has inherited his title and is now the sole proprietor of Tojo Ramen.
We know she's talking about Tsuneyo and not Wires-by-proxy because in the same thought she calls her a cottontail (i.e. child of a god and a mortal). In addition, she says that Tsuneyo has "ended up alone", implying she lost someone and further reinforcing the sole proprietor idea.


The notice of death is dated January 1. Tsuneyo's event "Thomas Mato, M.D." happens exactly one in-game week after Christmas, most likely* placing it on January 1.

[*] The Christmas party triggers on a Friday and "Thomas Mato, M.D." always triggers the next Friday. On the other hand, it's already January in Rin's event "Voice of Reason" and that happens in between the two. I think that's because Selebus screwed up the triggers, though; the trigger check for "Thomas Mato, M.D." is earlier in the code, implying it's supposed to happen first. Even if "Thomas Mato, M.D." doesn't happen on January 1, it's very soon afterward.

The time of death is in the morning and the event triggers in the evening, so it happens soon after Tsuneyo lost her father. The first line of the event refers to a deathbed, then we see Tsuneyo really going through it by Tsuneyo standards - ostensibly because of ghost rape, but I think there's more going on. After all, it's been a while since the rape at this point and she seemed completely fine at Christmas.
The repetition of "no one here at all" particularly stands out, fitting with the idea that Tsuneyo has ended up alone because her father died.

Later, a disembodied Tenchou-sama shows up to kick Kaori out of the store and Tsuneyo recognizes him as her dad.
Look at the tears in her eyes. That's the reaction of someone who thought she would never hear her dad's voice again, not someone who thinks he's bedridden upstairs.

I think this all fits with the idea that her dad recently died and she's grieving. Alternatively, if you think he's been dead the whole time, her state of mind could be because it's the anniversary of his death.
Mr. Tojo's physical body is dead, but it seems like Wires the god is still around. Although weakened, he lives on in a new host.
For Mr. Tojo, the name Tenchou-sama had a double meaning. Obviously he he was the manager of Tojo Ramen, but Wires is also the "manager" of the terminal. He's the one who fixes bugs, moderates access, resets it when things go wrong, etc. If Tsuneyo is the new tenchou, it could mean she - or an entity which is part of her - now has that role.

When Kaori talks about her "me inside of me", Tsuneyo implies that she has one of her own. This is the entity that made her start ranting about apostates in "TH15 15NT M3" - we're pretty sure it's Wires because he "claws his way out" right before it happens.

Which is referencing:
In "Denoument" there's an argument between Kaori's "me inside of me" and Tsuneyo's "me inside of me". In particular, "Kaori" represents USER3 in wanting Sensei to embrace comforting lies (you can see more with your eyes closed, stop looking for answers) and "Tsuneyo" represents USER2 in wanting Sensei to stop hiding from the truth (all you need to do is open your eyes).
(side note: I've begun to suspect that Pareidolia isn't the real USER3.)

In "Thomas Mato, M.D." Tsuneyo hears her dad's voice for the first time (based on her reaction). It probably wasn't the last. Later she claims he told her to take the day off. I think it would completely out of character for Tsuneyo to straight-up lie about this, so it's more likely she genuinely believes he told her that - even though he's not physically there.
Something inside Tsuneyo causes her to lose control and forcibly kiss Sensei, recreating what he did to Yumi in Chapter 1. In that earlier event, Wires's smile flashes on screen when Sensei loses control. Once again, Wires is recreating the memory of Sekai kissing Akira. (I'm not sure why - maybe he's glitching out, or maybe it's easier for him to force Tsuneyo to do something that corresponds to a real memory, even if it's not her own.)
He's probably feeding her supernatural information as well, whether intentionally or not. Sensei didn't tell her he met a god but somehow she still knew.

Here's a couple further hints from the narrator:
That opens the question of what exactly is happening to Tsuneyo and what it means for the future. There's not a lot to go off, but I'll throw out some thoughts.
Kaori's "me inside of me" is pretty clearly a second mind inside a single body. When Kaori is in control SeKaori is just a voice in her head, and presumably vice versa; the two consciousnesses are wholly distinct. And they also appear to have a mutual understanding; SeKaori may be able to seize control at times, but it doesn't seem like she's trying to eliminate Kaori's autonomy.

In contrast, Tsuneyo's relationship with her "me inside of me" seems a lot more antagonistic. She talks about how it forces her to do things against her will, and especially how it messes with her mind to accomplish this. She's tried to fight it off and reassert control (giving her a massive headache and making her pass out in "Yamato Nadeshiko"). Basically, Wires doesn't seem content with just "borrowing" her body on occassion, he wants to influence her own thoughts and actions as well. Just how far does he intend to go? Does he want to seize control of her body and maybe even overwrite her identity? Will it be a more symbiotic relationship where the two fuse into a combined consciousness where neither one dominates the other? Though I suppose it's possible his intentions really are completely benign, and Tsuneyo's issues are just inevitable consequences of integrating with a new host.

This also has me wondering about Mr. Tojo. The fact that Tsuneyo is a cottontail pretty much confirms that Wires is her dad, and the simplest way that makes sense is that they're the same person - either the mortal Mr. Tojo gained admin access to the terminal and became a god, or an admin of the terminal invented Mr. Tojo as a fictional identity to use inside of it. But maybe it's more complicated and they began as separate entities which later became integrated as one - the same thing Wires is currently attempting with Tsuneyo. That would help explain the apparent differences in their personalities - it's hard to reconcile the old Mr. Tojo (running illegal backroom gambling, possibly pressuring Sekai into sexual favors) with the technology god who dispassionately keeps things running smoothly.

I wanted to talk in depth about a few more topics from 0.52, but I'm not sure how many (if any) I'll get to before 0.53 drops. Here's some teasers:
1. The real(?) Ami and Maya have been missing since the last reset but will return to the story by Christmalloween at the latest.
2. Ami didn't kill Maya, [REDACTED] did.
3. My initial impression was wrong: Maya2 isn't Himawari, she is [REDACTED]. (This one is admittedly a stretch.)
4. The reveal that Himawari's name is Himawari conclusively proves that Himawari's name isn't Himawari.

spoilers.title: Part 1: Mr. Tojo is dead
spoilers.html:
We've known pretty much since the start of the game that Tsuneyo's father was going to die at some point - it's been repeatedly teased as a possibility. Here's one very explicit example from last Halloween:

0.52 contained strong evidence that he is in fact dead. It starts with the notice of death that is surrounded by USER2's trademark /////.
That image is shown directly after one which has two messages in the styles of USER1 and USER3, respectively.
Possibly the notice of death is meant to explain why there isn't also a message from USER2. In any case, it's connected to him in some way.

Then in "Denoument" some things are said by "Kaori" that heavily imply Mr. Tojo isn't around anymore. First she calls Tsuneyo "tenchou", which translates to manager. Previously, it was her dad that was called Tenchou-sama. The implication is she has inherited his title and is now the sole proprietor of Tojo Ramen.
We know she's talking about Tsuneyo and not Wires-by-proxy because in the same thought she calls her a cottontail (i.e. child of a god and a mortal). In addition, she says that Tsuneyo has "ended up alone", implying she lost someone and further reinforcing the sole proprietor idea.


The notice of death is dated January 1. Tsuneyo's event "Thomas Mato, M.D." happens exactly one in-game week after Christmas, most likely* placing it on January 1.

[*] The Christmas party triggers on a Friday and "Thomas Mato, M.D." always triggers the next Friday. On the other hand, it's already January in Rin's event "Voice of Reason" and that happens in between the two. I think that's because Selebus screwed up the triggers, though; the trigger check for "Thomas Mato, M.D." is earlier in the code, implying it's supposed to happen first. Even if "Thomas Mato, M.D." doesn't happen on January 1, it's very soon afterward.

The time of death is in the morning and the event triggers in the evening, so it happens soon after Tsuneyo lost her father. The first line of the event refers to a deathbed, then we see Tsuneyo really going through it by Tsuneyo standards - ostensibly because of ghost rape, but I think there's more going on. After all, it's been a while since the rape at this point and she seemed completely fine at Christmas.
The repetition of "no one here at all" particularly stands out, fitting with the idea that Tsuneyo has ended up alone because her father died.

Later, a disembodied Tenchou-sama shows up to kick Kaori out of the store and Tsuneyo recognizes him as her dad.
Look at the tears in her eyes. That's the reaction of someone who thought she would never hear her dad's voice again, not someone who thinks he's bedridden upstairs.

I think this all fits with the idea that her dad recently died and she's grieving. Alternatively, if you think he's been dead the whole time, her state of mind could be because it's the anniversary of his death.

spoilers.title: Part 2: Wires is inside of Tsuneyo now
spoilers.html:
For Mr. Tojo, the name Tenchou-sama had a double meaning. Obviously he he was the manager of Tojo Ramen, but Wires is also the "manager" of the terminal. He's the one who fixes bugs, moderates access, resets it when things go wrong, etc. If Tsuneyo is the new tenchou, it could mean she - or an entity which is part of her - now has that role.

When Kaori talks about her "me inside of me", Tsuneyo implies that she has one of her own. This is the entity that made her start ranting about apostates in "TH15 15NT M3" - we're pretty sure it's Wires because he "claws his way out" right before it happens.

Which is referencing:
In "Denoument" there's an argument between Kaori's "me inside of me" and Tsuneyo's "me inside of me". In particular, "Kaori" represents USER3 in wanting Sensei to embrace comforting lies (you can see more with your eyes closed, stop looking for answers) and "Tsuneyo" represents USER2 in wanting Sensei to stop hiding from the truth (all you need to do is open your eyes).
(side note: I've begun to suspect that Pareidolia isn't the real USER3.)

In "Thomas Mato, M.D." Tsuneyo hears her dad's voice for the first time (based on her reaction). It probably wasn't the last. Later she claims he told her to take the day off. I think it would completely out of character for Tsuneyo to straight-up lie about this, so it's more likely she genuinely believes he told her that - even though he's not physically there.

spoilers.html:
We've known pretty much since the start of the game that Tsuneyo's father was going to die at some point - it's been repeatedly teased as a possibility. Here's one very explicit example from last Halloween:
View attachment 5361169

0.52 contained strong evidence that he is in fact dead. It starts with the notice of death that is surrounded by USER2's trademark /////.
View attachment 5361171
That image is shown directly after one which has two messages in the styles of USER1 and USER3, respectively.
View attachment 5361172
Possibly the notice of death is meant to explain why there isn't also a message from USER2. In any case, it's connected to him in some way.

View attachment 5361174 View attachment 5361175 View attachment 5361176

The notice of death is dated January 1. Tsuneyo's event "Thomas Mato, M.D." happens exactly one in-game week after Christmas, most likely* placing it on January 1.

[*] The Christmas party triggers on a Friday and "Thomas Mato, M.D." always triggers the next Friday. On the other hand, it's already January in Rin's event "Voice of Reason" and that happens in between the two. I think that's because Selebus screwed up the triggers, though; the trigger check for "Thomas Mato, M.D." is earlier in the code, implying it's supposed to happen first. Even if "Thomas Mato, M.D." doesn't happen on January 1, it's very soon afterward.

posts.content_html_raw:
Summary of what happen during my absence :

Poem talking, Otoha with a penis (Bingoogus liked it), some more Maya = Himawari theories (with which I agree, of course! The drama!), people going crazy (again...), Sel's discord got hacked, Sel's getting corporate in Japan (What???), people going crazy (AGAIN????) and some ending theory.

Now that it's done, I can continue.
Since I have a folder with 1k pictures from the game, and some analysis, I decided to share with y'all one that I figure how to translate.
Maya and «Sensei», whose name is still unknown to us, were in a relationship during the «first loop», or the first one that Maya recalls. Unfortunately, after the «hard-drive saturation» of our protagonist, his memory was reset, wiping the sweet Maya from his mind. Traumatizing her.

Forlorn, listless, and still heartbroken, she keeps searching for the one she has lost, yet she fears that finding him again will only lead to losing him once more.

And precisely, she believes that our hero, or his current version, might be the «one» — the original. The one she once knew. But she's reluctant to tell him directly, preferring to stay low-key, even small, pushing him to forget her out of fear of bringing back his memories, «overloading his hard drive», and making him disappear. Again.
«Maya et "Sensei", puisque son nom nous est encore inconnu, étaient en relation lors de la "première boucle", ou la première dont Maya se souvient. Hélas, suite à la "saturation du disque dur" de notre protagoniste, la mémoire de ce dernier fut remise à zéro, effaçant ainsi de sa mémoire la douce Maya. Traumatisant cette dernière.

Renfrognée, désœuvrée et toujours le cœur brisée, elle ne cesse de chercher celui qu'elle a perdu, tout en ayant peur de le retrouver pour le perdre à nouveau.

Et justement, elle croit que notre héro, ou sa version actuelle, est potentiellement le "vrai". L'original. Celui qu'elle a jadis connu. Mais elle n'ose pas trop lui en dire, préférant se faire discrète, petite même, le poussant à l'oublier, par peur de lui faire revenir ses souvenirs, "surchargeant son disque dur", et de le faire disparaitre. À nouveau.»

And it made me laugh when I realize that, even at the beginning of the chapter two, I tough Maya prime might not be the «first».

Also, I took some time to think about the next update (not the Ayane epilogue, the one after) :
Yup. Maya.

I'm not gonna theorize about who she is/was, but about what come next about her.
Sel have four choices :
- Maya is definitively dead, so she won't be there anymore.
- A new Nu Maya will appear. (honestly, I hope it won't be... I want the story to advance, not stagnate!)
- Nu Maya return, like nothing happen.
- Maya prime return. (The easy choice...)

And, I don't know which one I prefer... they're all bad.

The first is as bad as the last (because, even if I want Maya prime back, it will feel... undeserved), so I'm stuck in my thinking, fearing what may come next.

That being said, I'll return into my cave, eating cold bland pasta, and waiting for the epilogue.

posts.content_html_raw:
Tin foil Maya thought:

Where did Maya come from?

There are a lot of juxtapositions with Maya being a "Normal teenage girl". However, every time her past is brought up before she meets Sensei its either vague or non-existent. Ami and the various narrators consistently say "She shouldnt be here" or "Doesn't exist" or something along those lines.

Pareidolia before leaving Sensei talks about how anything can become a god, and how the "worst punishment possible" for a god is to turn them human.

Maya always says she has the "Worst luck in the world".

All it takes is 1 believer to create a "god".

What if Sensei on the night he meets Maya, was in another desperate depression spiral. He wishes desperately for someone that can understand his situation.

Pareidolia says the gods had been watching Sensei and people like him.

What if they punished one of the gods in the bottom of the well? Creating "Maya".

This would create further parallels with the Altair and Vega story of star crossed lovers. Maya descends from the heavens, and she and Sensei fall in love.

Tin foil Maya thought:

Where did Maya come from?
Click to expand...
Nothing solid to add; just some gut feelings.
No matter how Maya gets described by others (ordinary girls or unexplainable entities alike), or how objectively strange her situation is, there is one trait of hers that always screams “human origin” to me and that is the fact that she plays violin, and she plays it so well that she gives Otoha an erection.

Many of her "things" are comical reliefs, hobbies that can be developed at a much later time, or just miscellaneous stuff that doesn't have the necessity to lead somewhere. Things like eating in the speed of light, watermelon fetish, and the love for stars but not in the strict astrophysics sense. Violin, however, needs practices, lessons, and time to master. In addition, the fact that she's good at only this particular instrument gives the feeling of a measly human practice rather than let's say, goddess of music or some kind who should've been born with much more comprehensive talents. More importantly, this feat isn't something I imagine Maya picked up after she met Akira, but perhaps a feat originated from a time before they met. If true, this would be a subtle support to the idea of Maya having a real, human origin.

Or maybe Maya really only picked up and mastered this hobby up at a much later time when she hid at Akira's tutoring apartment. Depending on how story unravels itself, this is not really too impossible. With how little we still know, however, I find it just a little easier to believe that Maya already knew how to play violin before she met him.

I'll throw my own towel into the theory-crafting game, and with all this talk recently about the gods using the human characters as hosts and some of the characters potentially being gods, I'll suggest that Maya is the god of strays. Her inability to remember anything about her life before meeting Akira may be an aspect of her godhood, and all the references to stray cats connected with her might just be metaphorical. As far as Sekai's disdain for Maya, it may be due to Maya having a completely different dynamic with Akira than any other character (potentially as an aspect of her godhood). We can see that Akira viewed Maya more as an equal than any of the other characters (both from his predatory advances towards her being turned on their head so early on in the story as well as Maya's long-term experience in the time loop acting as a guide for him). Whether that's because of Maya's personality or her aspect of godhood taking up so much of Akira's attention as part of being "adopted" into his household (literally or figuratively, it's kinda unclear), her dynamic with Akira is almost completely opposite of Sekai's dynamic with Akira and her expected behavior from him. Of course, if all three of these characters are gods (with or without knowing it), that makes this dynamic even more interesting...

Yeah, I think that'll be my pet theory I'll be running with for now.
