posts.content_html_raw:
I wanted to get in some predictions on upcoming events before the update drops. This post is a bit all over the place, but if there's an overarching theme it's figuring out what's going on with Ami and Maya and how it relates to the last reset and the current one. Please keep in mind this is mostly speculation based on cryptic foreshadowing, so it's very likely I've gotten things wrong. Edit: I finished writing this before seeing the 0.54 event list. The lack of Ami and Ayane events makes my predictions less likely, but I'm sharing them anyway.

Intro: There were two versions of Maya and Ami during the last reset. It's hinted that the ones who ended up in the post-reset world are less real than the pair who are missing.
Credit to DeSkel15, who pointed this out at the time:
DeSkel15 said:
Ami Prime specifically seemed to become a thing last Halloween. With the "Real Home" Ami seemingly being devoured by HOPE, while Ami Prime revealed herself and has been around since:

Why I refer to the Ami with Makoto as "Real Home" Ami is because Makoto had apparently ended up in the "real home":
View attachment 4911834 Narrator - "To the real home."
(Chapter 4 'All Around The Mulberry Bush' Main Event)

More Alt versions stuff for those interested:
Click to expand...
Here's my overview of what happens with the two versions of Ami and Maya:
Version #1: Maya and Ami start to head to the party and next thing we know Maya has been thrown back to Ch2 Halloween before jumping through time. She eventually wakes up in the "present" where Ami rapes her (though there are reasons to think this scene isn't entirely real). Ami claims that Maya blacked out before they ever got to the party and Ami carried her to the scary room. At the end of the rape scene, these characters supposedly die.
Version #2: After her TSS, Makoto returned to the present at the party. Shortly afterward, Maya and Ami arrive for the first time, intending to enact their threesome plan. Everyone except Makoto, Maya, and Ami pops out of existence and we don't see this Maya and Ami again.
Even if events are shown out of order, there's no way these happen in the same timeline. V1 Ami takes Maya directly to the scary room, they didn't go to the party first; and V2 are still friendly and planning to work together to seduce Sensei, the rape never happened for them.

After the reset Sensei ends up in a world where Ami and Maya have the memories of the V1 pair. But there are clues that V2 are at least as real:
  • The narrator says the place they (and Makoto) are in is the real home.
  • The rest of the class pops out of the real home. I think the implication is that they're being pulled from the previous world to where Sensei is now, which means the real home is the world everyone was in before the reset.
  • The arrival of V2 at the party follows directly from what we last saw from them before the reset started, whereas V1 Ami suddenly rejected her own threesome plan in favor of a sadistic rape that came completely out of nowhere and accomplished nothing.
  • There are inconsistencies in the V1 story that show something is not quite right: Maya (but not Ami) blacked out although she never has before, Ami and her noodle arms supposedly carried Maya to the room, and Maya inexplicably has the wrong haircut.
My conclusion is that V2 are the "real" Maya and Ami, who were last seen alone with Makoto at the party. The ones in the post-reset world are "fake" replacements. Ami could have been replaced by an Evil Ami (see the next section). But where did Maya's replacement come from? She certainly still thinks she's the same New Maya after the reset. Best theory I have is that there were two identical copies of New Maya, the same way that presumably happens when a wish creates a new world.
1. Sensei was warned in advance about Evil Ami's arrival during last Halloween, which only makes sense if she replaced the previous Ami.
This comes from what's probably the game's most cryptic event, "Arms Bent Back", most of which I still find completely inscrutable. However, I think some parts have started to make sense thanks to the benefits of hindsight. Most obviously, Moyo warned about the box containing Maya's head.
Just before this, Sensei is also warned about an entity that has almost caught up to him.
It's quite possible these two warnings are connected: the "extra pair of legs" and the "her" whose box he's not supposed to look into both refer to Evil Ami. Here's how that makes sense:
  • The warning about the entity is connected to the coming Halloween. That's when Evil Ami first shows up, killing Nodoka and raping Maya. (Not that it's certain that those two were the same Ami)
  • Evil Ami is an "extra pair of legs" in that she's an extra person: normal Ami is the one who should exist, Evil Ami is superfluous.
  • Other Senseis who the entity caught ended up "in the clouds", i.e. dead/erased/factory reset. Looking into Evil Ami's box threatens to do the same to Sensei.

The second part of the event (the rabbit family) makes clear that this is about a different Ami. We see an Ami who has her own Sensei - when our Sensei goes to her world, he's no longer "Sensei" there, he's nameless. This Ami also has two living parents, just like the Evil Ami who kills Nodoka. She says she's going to "move out" at Halloween.
Whether this is just foreshadowing or somehow something more real, I think this is showing how the Evil Ami from the alternate timeline is going to "move out" from her world and come to ours during the Halloween reset.
It's tempting to conclude that normal Ami never made it through the reset and Evil Ami replaced her completely, but I think it's more complicated than that. Since the reset, some events with Ami are clearly the evil version (basically whenever she talks to Maya), but Selebus has also continued to write events where Ami acts just like the insecure and jealous girl she's always been. For example, in this last update, her apology in "Natural Instinct" serves zero purpose in the story unless it's character development for the real Ami.

In fact, I think there's a very rigid set of criteria for when Evil Ami shows up, though I haven't looked back at events to confirm this.
  1. When she's alone with Maya, she acts like Evil Ami.
  2. When she's with Maya as well as other people, she pretends to be normal Ami, but she makes little effort to be convincing. Think of how aggressive she is when Maya and Sensei come to the dorm, or how she drops hints in front of Ayane that she knows about the resets.
  3. When she isn't around Maya, she's completely indistinguishable from normal Ami. If she's putting on an act, it's orders of magnitude better than the one she does when she's with Maya.
The only exception I can think of is when she threatens Niki with rape and murder in "Seed of Self-Doubt". But as I wrote about before, she's very unconvincing in her threats. It's like normal Ami is aware of Evil Ami's actions and is trying to claim them for herself to intimidate Niki.

So I think normal Ami is somehow still present, even if she isn't in complete control. The exact relation between her and Evil Ami is confusing, and I think we'll have to just wait to find out more.
2. Prediction: the original Ami and Maya from the last reset are still stuck in their version of Ayane's house. We'll see them again soon, probably in this update.
During the Halloween party, a narrator talked about girls getting stuck for "eternity" in the infinity house that is the Amamiya mansion. I think this is foreshadowing of what happened to the real Ami and Maya after the party.
At the D&D session which follows soon after Halloween we're given a hint that they're still out there. Ami and Maya aren't just absent from the session, we're pointedly told that their characters are away from the party on their own quest. (I think this event is full of foreshadowing - more on it in the next section.)
In the most recent update, Horseface Taki gave a hint about upcoming content which I think refers to this Ami and Maya.
They certainly are a pair of fan favorites who (if I'm right) have been missing for awhile, and there is an obvious parallel between infinity house and house of dreams. I think this also fits with the very small amount we (don't) know about upcoming content:
  • 0.54 is Christmalloween. Either there's going to be an unprecedented, abrupt time skip in the middle of the update, or Christmas and Halloween are going to happen "simultaneously" in two different timelines. Ami and Maya are in a different timeline and were last seen at Halloween.
  • Despite 0.54 being only about a month away, Selebus has yet to share the event list, implying that the list itself is a spoiler. The most obvious reason for that is he wouldn't want to reveal upcoming Maya events until the cliffhanger is resolved. (Edit: I was right about Maya events, but with only three of them and no Ami events, it's less likely this will be a major plotline.)

You may have noticed there's something I've avoided talking about: the last time we saw the "real" Ami and Maya, they were with Makoto as well. What happened to her? Horseface Taki mentions two girls, not three, and there haven't been any obvious hints that something is off about the Makoto in Sensei's post-reset world. To be honest, I have no good ideas here.
3. Prediction: Ayane is going to destroy the world to end the infinite spring.
First, let's establish why this needs to happen: as Himawari told us at the end of the last reset, the world is broken. Likely this is because of USER3's infinite spring.

...
When things went wrong in the last update, Himawari said she still intends to fix the world, but her final expression gives the impression that things are well and truly fucked.

If the world can't be fixed, the characters need to escape it somehow. That's where Ayane comes in, as foreshadowed in last Christmas's D&D session (Legacy of Thaum Pt. VI). While Ami and Maya are off in the "Western Sanctum" on their own quest, the rest of the party is trapped in an unending battle with Der Krampus, i.e. an evil god. I think this represents USER3 and his infinite spring.
The fight is only ended when Ayane destroys Der Krampus's snow globe, which holds a miniature world (infinite spring, infinite world). The girls then wake up in a new place (new world) with Santa (a... slightly less evil god? Wires? USER4?).
I'm not sure how exactly she's going to destroy the world, but there's a hint that she'll have to slip between planes/worlds to do it. That's the defining ability of a bird person, which she turns into as she seizes the snow globe.
A theme in LiL is breaking things completely as a first step to fixing them, and the "destruction is a form of creation" text implies it's the same for the world. Only by destroying one world is Ayane able to (indirectly) create a new one.
Replacing one world with another will be underwhelming unless there's something radically different about the new one. I can think of a couple of (not mutually exclusive) things that might be and which might be hinted at by the letter T.
  • Option 1: T is for Time. By destroying the world, Ayane also restarts the proper flow of time and ends the resets.
  • Option 2: T is for terminal. Ayane doesn't destroy one of the countless worlds within Terminal 23, but rather the entire thing. The new world where they wake up will be Terminal 24. After all, remember that this chapter started with Ami excited that the (infinite) spring would lead to "twenty-four".
One question I don't have an answer to: why are the girls older in the snow globe world? Does it have something to do with Ayane's epilogue and/or Himawari's world?

Tying everything together: last Halloween, Evil Ami was told she would have to wait for next year's Christmas (i.e. the now upcoming Christmalloween) and that SANTA was judging who was naughty or nice - just like the santas in both of the D&D worlds.
Possibly Ami and Maya lost in the infinity house will be the Halloween part of the update, and Ayane destroying the world will be the Christmas part. (Edit: this looks a lot less likely now that we know 0.54 contains a bunch of events for characters other than the trio.)
I ended up cutting a couple smaller parts of this post because I hit the attachment limit. I'll just throw out very briefly:
  • The broken world might date to the last beach trip, when the three moons showed up and Sensei "went for a swim", possibly ending up in the wrong world.
  • Maya's head in the box looks remarkably similar to how she looked at the moment the narrator said she "died" during the rape. I can't help thinking there's more of a connection here than just a simple visual repetition.

spoilers.title: Arms Bent Back and Evil Ami
spoilers.html:
This comes from what's probably the game's most cryptic event, "Arms Bent Back", most of which I still find completely inscrutable. However, I think some parts have started to make sense thanks to the benefits of hindsight. Most obviously, Moyo warned about the box containing Maya's head.
Just before this, Sensei is also warned about an entity that has almost caught up to him.
It's quite possible these two warnings are connected: the "extra pair of legs" and the "her" whose box he's not supposed to look into both refer to Evil Ami. Here's how that makes sense:
  • The warning about the entity is connected to the coming Halloween. That's when Evil Ami first shows up, killing Nodoka and raping Maya. (Not that it's certain that those two were the same Ami)
  • Evil Ami is an "extra pair of legs" in that she's an extra person: normal Ami is the one who should exist, Evil Ami is superfluous.
  • Other Senseis who the entity caught ended up "in the clouds", i.e. dead/erased/factory reset. Looking into Evil Ami's box threatens to do the same to Sensei.

The second part of the event (the rabbit family) makes clear that this is about a different Ami. We see an Ami who has her own Sensei - when our Sensei goes to her world, he's no longer "Sensei" there, he's nameless. This Ami also has two living parents, just like the Evil Ami who kills Nodoka. She says she's going to "move out" at Halloween.
Whether this is just foreshadowing or somehow something more real, I think this is showing how the Evil Ami from the alternate timeline is going to "move out" from her world and come to ours during the Halloween reset.

spoilers.title: Thoughts on Evil Ami
spoilers.html:
It's tempting to conclude that normal Ami never made it through the reset and Evil Ami replaced her completely, but I think it's more complicated than that. Since the reset, some events with Ami are clearly the evil version (basically whenever she talks to Maya), but Selebus has also continued to write events where Ami acts just like the insecure and jealous girl she's always been. For example, in this last update, her apology in "Natural Instinct" serves zero purpose in the story unless it's character development for the real Ami.

In fact, I think there's a very rigid set of criteria for when Evil Ami shows up, though I haven't looked back at events to confirm this.
  1. When she's alone with Maya, she acts like Evil Ami.
  2. When she's with Maya as well as other people, she pretends to be normal Ami, but she makes little effort to be convincing. Think of how aggressive she is when Maya and Sensei come to the dorm, or how she drops hints in front of Ayane that she knows about the resets.
  3. When she isn't around Maya, she's completely indistinguishable from normal Ami. If she's putting on an act, it's orders of magnitude better than the one she does when she's with Maya.
The only exception I can think of is when she threatens Niki with rape and murder in "Seed of Self-Doubt". But as I wrote about before, she's very unconvincing in her threats. It's like normal Ami is aware of Evil Ami's actions and is trying to claim them for herself to intimidate Niki.

So I think normal Ami is somehow still present, even if she isn't in complete control. The exact relation between her and Evil Ami is confusing, and I think we'll have to just wait to find out more.

spoilers.title: Lost in the infinity house
spoilers.html:
During the Halloween party, a narrator talked about girls getting stuck for "eternity" in the infinity house that is the Amamiya mansion. I think this is foreshadowing of what happened to the real Ami and Maya after the party.
At the D&D session which follows soon after Halloween we're given a hint that they're still out there. Ami and Maya aren't just absent from the session, we're pointedly told that their characters are away from the party on their own quest. (I think this event is full of foreshadowing - more on it in the next section.)
In the most recent update, Horseface Taki gave a hint about upcoming content which I think refers to this Ami and Maya.
They certainly are a pair of fan favorites who (if I'm right) have been missing for awhile, and there is an obvious parallel between infinity house and house of dreams. I think this also fits with the very small amount we (don't) know about upcoming content:
  • 0.54 is Christmalloween. Either there's going to be an unprecedented, abrupt time skip in the middle of the update, or Christmas and Halloween are going to happen "simultaneously" in two different timelines. Ami and Maya are in a different timeline and were last seen at Halloween.
  • Despite 0.54 being only about a month away, Selebus has yet to share the event list, implying that the list itself is a spoiler. The most obvious reason for that is he wouldn't want to reveal upcoming Maya events until the cliffhanger is resolved. (Edit: I was right about Maya events, but with only three of them and no Ami events, it's less likely this will be a major plotline.)

You may have noticed there's something I've avoided talking about: the last time we saw the "real" Ami and Maya, they were with Makoto as well. What happened to her? Horseface Taki mentions two girls, not three, and there haven't been any obvious hints that something is off about the Makoto in Sensei's post-reset world. To be honest, I have no good ideas here.

spoilers.title: Der Krampus and the snow globe
spoilers.html:
First, let's establish why this needs to happen: as Himawari told us at the end of the last reset, the world is broken. Likely this is because of USER3's infinite spring.

...
When things went wrong in the last update, Himawari said she still intends to fix the world, but her final expression gives the impression that things are well and truly fucked.

If the world can't be fixed, the characters need to escape it somehow. That's where Ayane comes in, as foreshadowed in last Christmas's D&D session (Legacy of Thaum Pt. VI). While Ami and Maya are off in the "Western Sanctum" on their own quest, the rest of the party is trapped in an unending battle with Der Krampus, i.e. an evil god. I think this represents USER3 and his infinite spring.
The fight is only ended when Ayane destroys Der Krampus's snow globe, which holds a miniature world (infinite spring, infinite world). The girls then wake up in a new place (new world) with Santa (a... slightly less evil god? Wires? USER4?).
I'm not sure how exactly she's going to destroy the world, but there's a hint that she'll have to slip between planes/worlds to do it. That's the defining ability of a bird person, which she turns into as she seizes the snow globe.
A theme in LiL is breaking things completely as a first step to fixing them, and the "destruction is a form of creation" text implies it's the same for the world. Only by destroying one world is Ayane able to (indirectly) create a new one.
Replacing one world with another will be underwhelming unless there's something radically different about the new one. I can think of a couple of (not mutually exclusive) things that might be and which might be hinted at by the letter T.
  • Option 1: T is for Time. By destroying the world, Ayane also restarts the proper flow of time and ends the resets.
  • Option 2: T is for terminal. Ayane doesn't destroy one of the countless worlds within Terminal 23, but rather the entire thing. The new world where they wake up will be Terminal 24. After all, remember that this chapter started with Ami excited that the (infinite) spring would lead to "twenty-four".
One question I don't have an answer to: why are the girls older in the snow globe world? Does it have something to do with Ayane's epilogue and/or Himawari's world?

Tying everything together: last Halloween, Evil Ami was told she would have to wait for next year's Christmas (i.e. the now upcoming Christmalloween) and that SANTA was judging who was naughty or nice - just like the santas in both of the D&D worlds.
Possibly Ami and Maya lost in the infinity house will be the Halloween part of the update, and Ayane destroying the world will be the Christmas part. (Edit: this looks a lot less likely now that we know 0.54 contains a bunch of events for characters other than the trio.)

Should I play this game?

After reading many reviews of the game I don't know if this gonna be a perfect game for me or some massive waste of time, so please give your honest opinion, because for now I land right in the middle. (I figure you guys can be huge fan but please I'm not looking for entering a new sect for now, I just need honesty.)

What I like:

Long games with deep stories. I'm more looking for a great narration and some lewd scenes than the other way around.
I'm a sensitive fella but not everything need to be rainbow in paradise (even tho love™ is a wonderful thing). I really enjoyed Pale Carnation & Being a DIK recently because my suspension of disbelief of over the top, I was wrapped in the story and interactions in those games.

posts.content_html_raw:
If incest is a no-go, and if following a guide mod (it's an in-game one) are deal-breakers, then no. Lessons in Love is a story about the cycle of sexual abuse, and how it destroyed and keeps destroying people's lives. It is technically a porn game, but it's unlikely you'll find many sex scenes tailored for that reason. The tone of most of them is just disturbing from the overall context, even if the larger part is "wholesome" (to the extent that it can be).

So, while it does fullfil your requirements of an engaging and thought out story, where things happen for a reason, it's up to you if having a thought provoking story about things you don't like is enough to make you want to give it a shot or not.

At the end of the day, this is a very unique game. My personal opinion is that you should give it a try for a couple of hours and see if the writing captivates you. One last point of relevance is about you not liking long games... well, this would immediately fail this one, since a playthrough of the current content takes around 6 weeks for most people.

Edit: Maybe try "Out of Touch" for a much "safer" thought out story (still long though).

The game is sandbox based with affection and lust grinding and I wouldn't be surprised if it's responsible for a bunch of other games using the same sandbox method.

There's a guide mod which I would say is required to play with. If you don't have the time to play the 180 hour game 3 times then use the guide mod to play the game in a way where you don't miss any events, strong evidence to show it's the true path (although there is some interesting dialogue in the wrong choices very occasionally)

There's a puzzle guide in the OP. If you want you can try to solve the puzzles yourself. You'll have to start taking notes of weird numbers or odd pieces of detail in the dialogue or pictures. Just make sure to properly read the guide, there's at least one puzzle in the game that puts in a bit of work to punish you for solving the puzzle with a guide without actually having done the ingame work to have solved the puzzle legitimately, and the game pulls similar tricks for other events, marks you as a cheater and deletes your affection scores and prevents you seeing important lore scenes.

URM is a great utility mod for this game, making it easy to change certain variables and it lets you see where 98% of the game splits due to choices made and grinding that you have or haven't done. I don't recommend it due to how easy it is to brick your save because people don't stop going down paths they didn't earn. View the dialogue if you want, but then always roll back before it and go where your save file says you've gone. Do not use the ingame cheat menu to cheat your stats, use URM if you have to. There's only one cheat code you should maybe use and you shouldn't until you've got up to the current update or otherwise know what the current content is.

If you get pissed off at the grinding there is an autoVN mod that turns the game into a linear story and it gives you the affection you need. I haven't seen complaints about bugs for this, and I know the guide mod has some issues even if it's like 95% good. You miss out on the sandbox lust grinding and animations / dialogue but you can also disable the mod in the menu and get back to the sandbox whenever you want. It's pretty well done.



I'd say you should play it, but if you get to the creepy events I was talking about and your gut says nope nope i'm out, trust it and move on.

Long games with deep stories. I'm more looking for a great narration and some lewd scenes than the other way around.

I mean, it sounds like it's up your alley. There's a few specific scenes I can think of that sound like they might push you out of your comfort zone but they're not there for shits and giggles, they have a point and make sense within the context of the story.

Cringe: I wouldn't say there are really any "cringe" or edgy characters in LiL. There's a singular event chain that springs to mind as far as cringe humour goes but that's pretty inconsequential and skippable in the grand scheme of a 160-200 hour game. The MC is a 30 year old dude himself and he's a mopey fuck but not "edgy".

Sadism: Sensei's weapon of choice is his massive penis. There isn't really much overt physical violence in the game period, and what there is has a point or else makes sense in the context - I can only really think of one very short scene that had me thinking "was that necessary, really?" but again, drop in the ocean relatively speaking.

Bad horror/cheap fantasy/etc.: I wouldn't really say LiL falls into the category of bad or cheap horror but that's a pretty subjective thing.

Incest/raceplay: There's definitely incest in LiL but it's mostly avoidable if you really want and even if you choose to play with it, it's pretty integral to the story and not all like..."ahhh oni-chan" hentai-fied

On balance I'd second what Moony said and encourage you to just give it a few hours - despite the length I think most people who enjoy LiL probably found themselves captivated quite quickly, and the author was quite clever in that he puts a couple of the weirder/more disturbing scenes early on so that people would be able to figure out relatively quickly if it wasn't for them.

And if you do give it a go absolutely use the walkthrough mod or the AVN mod lol

Drama and mystery is this author's bread and butter. He is great at getting you to feel for the characters, even ones you originally start off apathetic about. As a personal anecdote:
After the first part of the story that sets everything up and establishes some sort of status quo, there are new characters that begin to be added pretty abruptly. I remember finding myself feeling a bit wary and annoyed at the time because I didn't trust the author to have enough time or care to actually flesh them out if he kept on repeating this. Needless to say, some of them are my favorite characters now...

Cringe/awkward edgyness: There are a few cringe pop cultural and personal references but it never gets nearly as cringe as "skibidi" or the like. The author is in his
30s as well, so I think you have a good chance of getting his humor.
Even at it's worst it's never common enough to really get overbearing imo.

Sadistic or hurting others for the sake of it: it happens in the story but not necessarily from the MC. He does in fact feel remorse at times (doesn't automatically make him a good person for it) but he's not a sadistic, violent murder/rapist or anything.

Cheap fantasy/bad horror: I think you'll be fine here. The "horror" aspect of the game comes across as more of a... symbolic manifestation of trauma than actual plot-relevant set piece that is meant to make you scared. Some of it is purposely wacky to the point of comedy, some of it invokes a tragic and somber feeling for what it seems to represent.

Incest is absolutely core to the story and personal character arcs, but it's not there simply for catering to a kink (most of the time.)

Anyways, if you can handle a bit of dark subjects treated in a somewhat serious manner (with some jokes spread out here and there to lighten the mood and poke at the obvious) I think this story might be worth a shot.

posts.content_html_raw:
In celebration of Halloween, I wrote up one more spoooOOOooky theory to squeeze in before the update.

Ami didn't kill Maya. Sensei unwittingly killed her while he was blacked out.

(Sorry, when I said "spooky", I actually meant depressing as fuck.)
Maya's death happens during Tsuneyo's event "Denoument". This is confirmed by "Tsuneyo" and "Kaori" commenting on Sensei's poor timing in bringing up his love for bird girl Maya.
Just before this, Nao starts trying to warn Sensei that something bad is happening.
And shortly after the comments about Sensei's poor timing, Nao becomes resigned that she can no longer stop what's happening.
The simple explanation is that Ami is about to kill Maya somewhere else, Nao senses it, and she tries to snap Sensei out of his blackout so that he can go save her. I don't think that's what happening though; she's actually trying to stop Sensei himself from doing something. The proof is in the noodles.
The basic idea is that Sensei killed Maya while blacked out in "Denouement", but his brain and/or the gods tricked him into thinking he was just eating a bowl of ramen.

The timing of Nao's warning is very important. She starts pulling Sensei's sleeve just as the bowl of ramen is placed in front of him.
Notice also the figure in the upper left - looks like it could be a hogtied Maya. That doesn't necessarily mean that she's really there (it could be a symbol/hallucination), but it's still suggestive in linking her to the ramen.

Nao becomes much more animated in trying to stop Sensei when he suggests she share the "ramen" with him. She really doesn't like the idea that Sensei is going to "eat" it.
And she abruptly gives up on trying to stop him right after he finally chows down, as the gods look on and laugh maniacally.
Two other notes here: 1. "Eating the ramen" has a big enough emotional impact on Sensei that he feels like he got hit by a car. 2. Afterwards, all three characters repeat that Sensei is someone who "shows up and takes" - by eating the soup, he took something away from someone else.

Sensei initially went to the ramen-ya to eat a bird instead of kissing one. The bird he normally kisses is Maya, but this time he's going to "eat" her.
And this is reinforced when he sees Maya's head. The trauma causes his brain to snap into defense mode, he hallucinates that Maya's head is actually a bunch of noodles, and he quite literally starts trying to eat them. He's continuing the same dinner he was "served" at the ramen shop.
Earlier in the day, Yasu warned New Maya that something bad would happen to her if she stuck around.
The warning is intriguingly vague (she never specifies that "here" is the beach or that "bad things" is death), but most likely it's about Maya's death during "Denouement". Yasu says she doesn't want to hear it happen.
At least on the previous day, Yasu could only hear Sensei's actions.
So there's a good chance she wouldn't hear Maya's death if Ami dragged her off and killed her in private, but she would definitely hear it if Sensei killed her.
I should probably address the "shared dream" nature of "Denouement". That means that nothing it shows is guaranteed to actually be happening. Maybe Sensei symbollically destroyed Maya at the same time that Ami killed her for real. That could represent his guilt over all of the bad things that have happened to her, including his inability to stop Ami this time. I don't really buy that, though, because of Nao's actions. She's a bystander to the shared dream, observing the other three's poetry but not caught up in it, so she's seeing what's really happening. She sees Sensei about to do something and tries to stop him.

Another possibility is that Maya is already dead (thanks to Ami) and Sensei does something bad to her body. But keep in mind that Nao tries to stop him out of compassion, which to me implies a living victim. If he kills Maya, it also explains why Nao so suddenly gives up - Maya died and Nao could no longer do anything. If Maya is already dead, I don't know what else would cause Nao's abrupt change.
There are more things to discuss, such as how Maya got there and Sensei's (subconscious) motive, but those will have to wait until next month. Hint: the RAS meeting wasn't the first time Maya2 showed up in the update. I'll bring this up again after the 0.53 discussion dies down.

I think this is more likely, because I have a better moment when I think Maya was killed. Makoto's "A Matter of Time".

Maya is in the event earlier, Makoto is trying to get her to the RAS party. Ami shows up, scary red light, Maya is convinced to leave with her. Then the narrator brings up the colors, talking about how they are misdirection, a trick of perception, then they talk about Makoto and Yumi on the beach, the narrator starts crashing out about this, then there's a static jump where this screenshot is from, with dialogue written in a cheesy foreshadowing way.


Before there's a lot of static white flash and color flashing off as the narrator is cut off, figuratively and I think literally too. The narrator dialogue stops there and its just dialogue between Yumi and Makoto.

With the time shenanigans going on / Sel not thinking about everything 100% of the time, I doubt there's any thoughts to decomposition but maybe she recognises the smell of a dead body that Akira just bathed himself in.

That's why whatever the smell is, that I don't think it's actual smell of death / decomposition (or Sel hasn't thought about it enough)

If this happened in real life, it probably wouldn't have had enough time to decay even under ideal conditions, but that's why I don't think Tsuneyo's dad's corpse is rotting either. I couldn't point out what the smell should be, it doesn't make sense compared to real life. But it is the clues I've been given.

shmurfer said:
I think this is more likely, because I have a better moment when I think Maya was killed. Makoto's "A Matter of Time".

Maya is in the event earlier, Makoto is trying to get her to the RAS party. Ami shows up, scary red light, Maya is convinced to leave with her. Then the narrator brings up the colors, talking about how they are misdirection, a trick of perception, then they talk about Makoto and Yumi on the beach, the narrator starts crashing out about this, then there's a static jump where this screenshot is from, with dialogue written in a cheesy foreshadowing way.

View attachment 5397755

Before there's a lot of static white flash and color flashing off as the narrator is cut off, figuratively and I think literally too. The narrator dialogue stops there and its just dialogue between Yumi and Makoto.

We've long talked about how characters have been narrators, and I think this was a tip of the hat to how Maya definitely was one of them.



As for why Nao-chan stops him. Nao-chan specifically isn't shown to talk in a pretentious all knowing way, she's quite down to earth when she has the notepad and tries to help in simple ways. I think she saw he was served a part of Maya, and she was trying to get him to break the perception trick being played on him to no success. Once the meal is done there's no need for her to struggle anymore, she's just frowning and the people posessing the other girls are laughing and insulting Nao, comparing her to Sensei.

I think it's doubly true if you look at the end of the event where they get their minds back. Tsuneyo recognises the scent of what's on him. You've already theorized that you think Tsuneyo's dad is dead, and his corpse is in Tojo Ramen and there's a smell to it. With the time shenanigans going on / Sel not thinking about everything 100% of the time, I doubt there's any thoughts to decomposition but maybe she recognises the smell of a dead body that Akira just bathed himself in.
Click to expand...
"Matter of Time": I'm going to have to assert this without proof for now, but I'm almost certain the Maya in this event (the one who goes off alone with Ami) is Maya2, not the one who dies. (Doesn't mean you're wrong about the narrator)

Cannibalism: In "Cities in Gifu" Nao is unbothered when Sensei shows the head and says it's some noodles that he intends to eat. I think it's unlikely she would be so agitated on the first occasion and then care not even a little bit about whether he continues to eat more. (Unless it's already too late. Now that Sensei has had his first taste of human flesh, he'll do anything to experience it again. The rest of the game is just him hunting down the girls like animals... But he's still hungry. He will always be hungry.)

Smell: This one is ambiguous. As you say, Tojo Ramen smelling like death is a recurring plot point. But in the event immediately prior to this one, Nao (through Kaori) says that Tsuneyo's home smells like pork broth. So a completely innocent explanation is possible. Arguably, though, neither one makes much sense - no actual ramen was consumed, and a fresh body isn't going to smell anything like a rotting corpse.

posts.content_html_raw:
Will be interesting to see how Sel handles the pacing from this point on, will be huge whiplash to return to the sandbox/chapter 4 and before normal at any point after this update. While the game still has 5(?) years left until completion per his own timeline, things seem to be reaching a boiling point that would require a somehow bigger revelation than the things spoken plainly in this update to bring that boiling point back down to a sizzle; if in the next 5 years the story returns to the old pacing, it will either be well done because of something currently not present in narrative, or it will be simply bad.

While a lot that was revealed was both foreshadowed and theorized in some form by the community, and reading the recent story with that in mind didn't detract too much from it, by stating it outright in the text itself to not only the characters but any and all readers, Sel has sort of locked himself into future text reflecting the revelations, lest readers lose interest from the whiplash. Treading water with some character arcs for the sake of others, or some characters not having events/focus for months to years irl isn't gonna work after this update, and it barely did before.

A few thoughts about the update:

First, a bunch of memes:
1. "Himawari's responsible for everything and she has been secretly planning everything since forever!" says the chat for years now:


2. Selebus direct response to reading the thread being pissed at Akira for years:

Quick flash of literal imaginary waifu granted physical form

Other screenshots:

Now my notes on the huge amount of lore:
So, to reiterate what we know:

01 - Akira 1 wished for Maya, which made Maya be created in a secondary universe for Akira 2. That Maya wished for TERMINAL 23, which I'm assuming is a world where Akira didn't kill himself. But because she's a wish herself, the fact that her wish was granted shouldn't be possible, which is why Kumon mi is all fucked up, it's faulty basically.

She herself is made to be all about sex and forbidden things, which I assume also has to do with why Kumon mi's is all sexual and keen to fuck Akira. It's likely that everyone's being influenced by her very nature, which was a wish fullfilment for Akira in the first place.

While this ocurrence draws the attention of Himawari's company, over time they lose interest because it loses its novelty. It's possible that Maya's life being hell is a mixture of them prodding her to try to understand this anomaly, or just the result of the anomaly itself.

02 - Ami is aware of the resets, and is likely protected by a god, that being either Sekai (most likely), or maybe Nozomu? The company tries to deal with her for good through various methods, and is implied that Shiori has tried to kill her as well - although it is also implied she's more than likely to end her own life to escape the erasing of memories. It is also confirmed that Ami goes around killing people, and will even kill Akira.

She simply does not want to leave this world, which is why she fakes it. But even when she is reset, her memories come back after a time (kind of explaining why sometimes Ami truly doesn't know things, until she finally remembers). Also, it is revealed that Ami is actively running away during resets every time.

03 - Himawari's company, likely the Shiawase group, exists as an intermediary between humans and gods, and tries to facilitate the granting of wishes. But the bureaucracy is insane in terms of maintaning the created worlds, and is also bizarre in the sense that the one making the wish doesn't get to enjoy it. Himawari's plan is to create her own company that allows for people to vacation in multiple dream worlds (which is VERY likely what the purity routes are).
04 - Still on the Shiawase company, it employs custodians, like Himawari and Shiori, whose job is to "clean" each world between resets by resetting memories. Most worlds continue for a much longer amount of time than Kumon mi, and aren't nearly as bizarre. The easy part of the job is just resetting people in a doll like state, but it is implied that they may have to fight from time to time as well.

05 - Himawari started working at the company so that she could better the lives of her parents, though we're not informed as to what happened to them. When Akira asks her why not simply wait for history to run its course since she's proof that they eventually succeed, she says that she wants to diminish their suffering before and after she's born, and also maybe it has to do with investigating how to eventually create the Himawari co. (with purity routes) for real.

06 - Himawari's wish was for creating a pocket dimension where she spends her everyday with her parents, and the experiences she has there go back to her. This is likely to be the prototype purity route, meaning that eventually, Akira will be able to live a full life with each of the girls (on their purity route) and those experiences will flow back into him (thus enabling the green route).

07 - Himawari has to erase the memories of her from both her parents because, although ultimately those memories power leveled them to where they were in order to escape the simulation, that would fizzle without them actually going through the motions to get there. Thus making it even riskier for them to arrive at their shared wished for conclusion (since the first time they obviously didn't have future knowledge of their unborn daughter).

08 - Himawari has to leave TERMINAL 23 behind and cannot interfere anymore. From now on, Shiori will be in charge of her duties, since she's interested in who Nodoka is, being acquainted with Kyoko (her mother), who apparently looks just like her.

09 - The company does not control everything that have to do with the reset, like the position in which the people reawaken. This apparently is decided by the world itself. And a lot of gods talking in people's heads, according to Himawari is nothing more than unsolicited advertisement. It's not like these gods have power or are actively controlling things, they are simply selling a service while withholding information.

To sum up: Maya is a wish and TERMINAL 23 is her own wish. Ami is being actively protected by an unsanctioned god, and is an enemy of the company, constantly losing and getting her memories back with each reset at different times. Himawari is the actual daughter of Ayane and Akira, and as canon as canon can be in this story (since she works in the company). Himawari is out from any further interference and Shiori is in.
Finally, I thought it was an amazing update that really needed to happen. I have been questioning Selebus writing on multiple fronts for a while now, and it was a good decision to stop creating more bullshit and actually ground the story with a lot of lore drops.

It was also incredibly wholesome and to give both Akira and the player a notion of who he will become, including loving his daughter in a healthy way, and actively rejecting cheating on his wife is also very welcomed. On its own, a 9/10 update (Himawari is amazing), but against the quality of chapter 4, 10/10. Good work, Selebus.

Ami is being actively protected by an unsanctioned god, and is an enemy of the company, constantly losing and getting her memories back with each reset at different times. posts.content_html_raw:
This is the second post on lore, but this one is just on the reevaluation of what we already knew. Especially on Maya and Kumon-mi.
So, basic facts: Maya one day dropped onto Akira's lap, an Akira that did not wish for her. This will be relevant.

Akira 1 wished for Maya in World A. Akira 2 received Maya unsolicited in World B. They lived in that world where Maya was this little girl made for him in every possible way , and something happened that made her wish for TERMINAL 23. That was very likely his suicide because, otherwise, Maya would have no reason to wish for an eternal world of repeating the same year over and over.

Following basic rules, the Maya born into that world would also not be the Maya that wished for it. So now we have the Maya and Akira of TERMINAL 23 (which is World C). Basically, the company went "wtf, what is this world created by a wish? we need to observe and see what is going on."

Because Maya was, to begin with, a wish from Akira - that means that, although 23 is her world, it is also a world created to suit Akira, placing him in the center of it - but not as the protagonist, but as an object. This is likely what NAO was talking about when she said he was not the protagonist. Maya is the actual protagonist and Akira is an instrument to prod and test Maya to try to figure out what is this anomaly.

Through thousands of years, the company took care of 23, and put gods in charge to try to figure things out through various methods. In each cycle of resets they ran experiments and often held even tv shows since "the anomaly" captured a lot of people's attention. Gods would even likely be interested in taking people there for a ride in order to experience for themselves what is up with this strange and unique world. They would observe what changed the "puppet Akira", and how Maya reacted to it, trying to find the missing link to understanding how it was possible for her to create the anomaly.

After a very long time, the gods and the company itself started to lose interest because they couldn't figure things out, and it was proving to be more trouble than it was worth (especially with Ami). With the approaching end of its run (the well is nearly dry), a secondary anomaly happened. Our Akira entered 23.

Our Akira is not from 23. It's not just that he recalls things, it's that all previous Akiras were not him (but the puppet Akiras born from Maya's wish and used by the company to test her), which is why Himawari is trying to get him out of there alongside her mom.

Well, we're not sure who our Akira is. Maybe he's the Akira from World B, the one that got Maya and eventually killed himself. If he's that one, then Maya recognizing him would mean that he's the one she made her wish for. The one she should never have met in 23, because in 23 there should only be Akiras made from her wish. In fact, the Maya from 23 shouldn't even be the Maya that made the wish, so how could she recognize him in the first place?

Himawari says the company still doesn't understand lots of things about this world and has largely given up on it. Everything we have seen so far regarding gods has either been them trying to create a set of circumstances that advances their understanding of the anomaly (so that they can get a higher rating at the company), or to fullfil their own needs (either existencial or personal).

It is unknown if all the gods interfering are under the company though, because the world itself doesn't seem to be. And 23 is very much so an anomaly. I've seen someone mention the TSSs, and the possible answer is that because 23 is going down, the gods are trying to get a wish from people before the end. Akira and Maya are no-go, since they have already used theirs. But the other can still make contracts, and everything in 23 is overly sexual because of Maya.

Ami is an interesting case because she either has a contract that puts her beyond the reach of even "peerless gods", like HOPE himself. Or it's even more terrifying and she's protected to that extent without a contract. It's odd that the same protection does not extend to protecting her from custodians (which are below gods in the first place).
These were a few things I thought about from getting the info on Maya. I'm sure a lot can be further examined, but this is preliminary.

In each cycle of resets they ran experiments and often held even tv shows since "the anomaly" captured a lot of people's attention. Gods would even likely be interested in taking people there for a ride in order to experience for themselves what is up with this strange and unique world. They would observe what changed the "puppet Akira", and how Maya reacted to it, trying to find the missing link to understanding how it was possible for her to create the anomaly.
After a very long time, the gods and the company itself started to lose interest because they couldn't figure things out, and it was proving to be more trouble than it was worth (especially with Ami). With the approaching end of its run (the well is nearly dry), a secondary anomaly happened.
Our
Akira entered 23.
Our Akira
is not from 23
. It's not just that he recalls things, it's that all previous Akiras were not him (but the puppet Akiras born from Maya's wish and used by the company to test her), which is why Himawari is trying to get him out of there alongside her mom.
Well, we're not sure who our Akira is. Maybe he's the Akira from World B, the one that got Maya and eventually killed himself. If he's that one, then Maya recognizing him would mean that he's the one she made her wish for. The one she should never have met in 23, because in 23 there should only be Akiras made from her wish. In fact, the Maya from 23 shouldn't even be the Maya that made the wish, so how could she recognize him in the first place?
Himawari says the company still doesn't understand lots of things about this world and has largely given up on it. Everything we have seen so far regarding gods has either been them trying to create a set of circumstances that advances their understanding of the anomaly (so that they can get a higher rating at the company), or to fullfil their own needs (either existencial or personal).
It is unknown if all the gods interfering are under the company though, because the world itself doesn't seem to be. And 23 is very much so an anomaly. I've seen someone mention the TSSs, and the possible answer is that because 23 is going down, the gods are trying to get a wish from people before the end. Akira and Maya are no-go, since they have already used theirs. But the other can still make contracts, and everything in 23 is overly sexual because of Maya.
Ami is an interesting case because she either has a contract that puts her beyond the reach of even "peerless gods", like HOPE himself. Or it's even more terrifying and she's protected to that extent without a contract. It's odd that the same protection does not extend to protecting her from custodians (which are below gods in the first place).

posts.content_html_raw:
Wow yeah, phenomenal update. I cried several times and I'm not ashamed to admit it. I knew I was onto something when referencing this story as having a hopeful undertone despite all of the suffering.

Life is full of suffering, but as long as you persevere then all the darkness just makes the good things that much more impactful.

As for discussion on the "true canon waifu" of the story, I personally think it's a bit more complicated than it seems...
Obviously this arc is focused on her and Selebus himself has a certain fondness for Ayane, but I still believe that this update shows just ONE possibility of the world that Maya created. That's not to say that she isn't special in some way since Himawari is playing such an important role, but the flash of Maya taking Ayane's place during the pocket wish seems to imply that it could've (and possibly has/will/should've depending on how Maya's world really works) been Maya or someone else.
I still think the core plot device of this story is going to loop back to Maya's wish in the end. Her paradoxical box of wonders seems to be breaking every convention that the higher powers seem to be aware of, and I think even they are underestimating its true potential. After all, a"fake" person born from a wish creating their own wish conceptually makes them "real" does it not? If a wish can become reality and affect other worlds, destinies, and even create people when it's not supposed to, then that might be something that breaks apart everything established up til now.
Including....dare I say being the key to making Himawari's dream possible? It really adds even more reasoning to Himawari's involvement in this world and her willingness to take these risks.
In addition, as much as we are in the honey-moon phase of sorts about Ayane's blissful possible future and finally experiencing HOPE first hand, couldn't it be even more poetic and if Akira's wish, the imaginary girl that he created seemingly to save him from his loneliness and trauma, defied all logic and paradoxically became real enough to become the thing that breaks him out of his cycle of trauma/the world he's stuck in and as well as even possibly the co-facilitator for the possible true ending of Himawari's idealized wishing device? Seeing the potential future of him having an amazing daugher like Himawari is enough to make Akira prouder than we've ever seen him and make strides in his self-worth, what if the actual manifestation of his traumas becomes the one thing that saves others and allows their dreams become true as well? Would that do something in proving to himself that he's not beyond saving?

T stands for trauma. It can cripple and destroy you, or it can turn you into something great by overcoming it.

Obviously this is all wild speculation and thematic pondering but goddamnit if this update doesn't have my head absolutely swimming with all sorts of questions and possibilities. Bravo, Selebus.

I may finally do my first full reread after this update, first started reading when update .35 was the newest, catching up to what was then current content a week before .36 released.

Part of what is tempting me to do so is the desire to try to gleam what exactly about T23 is anomalous. This update itself mentioned some things, Moonflare summarized above, but part of me feels that given what we learn this update that there is earlier supernatural stuff earlier on that occurs that is also unique to T23 that hasn't been stated clearly.

Specifically, I'm interested in revisting both Naos that appear in the story, as well as The Old One. As far as i remember, of the many gods/major entities in the story, the only ones that were introduced before Chapter 4 were HOPE, Wires, Paradoliea, and The Old One. The Chapter 1 rewrite occurs mid Chapter 3 iirc, may be fair to assume that Sel solidified parts of this company idea during that time as The Chapter 1 rewrite inserts Himi into events like The Room With Clocks. I am of the opinion without actually looking back at the text that both Naos and The Old One are the type of anomalies unique to t23, and more than just trying to identify what makes T23 unique compared to "normal" worlds I'm also interested at revisiting every "reset", the lead up and events, as when Sensei watched Himi work we learned partly what actually happens in t23 while the RAS gets "sent to do puzzles" or "blacks out." In particular I am very interested in whether or not Ami did that to herself right before the reset in .35 or if something else did; with what we know what other thing would be motivated and able to do that to her? And could she really have done it herself?

Additionally, with Nao's appearance in that one happy event, I think that until given reason to believe otherwise that the supposed protection provided to Ami from a power that rivals "a peerless god" is from "the world." Himi states that the company is not in control of the world itself, is why she doesn't know where everyone is right away. If "the world" is able to be free from control of the company, it stands to reason that Ami, who "provides challenges" for the company, is related to "the world," and I personally don't think that Sekai is the world in this and most other contexts.

Ok... just finished this update and... oh lord, it was difficult.
Not in an emotional plan though (not much, at least), but mainly on a «cerebral» plan? Intellectual? I don't know how to spell it, but I'm gonna talk, a little bit, about the elephant in the church :
I'm obliged, of course, because there's so much questions about her, and the first is about her tangibility.

So, from what I understand (and if she tell us the whole truth), Maya's a Sensei wish, and the world is a wish of Maya (which isn't supposed to be allowed... alright.) But, since Himawari told us that, that world is what allow Ayane and Sensei to conceive her, so she is the result (or a form of) of the wish from a wish?

Is it just me or... it doesn't make any sense? It seems to imply that Maya must exist (and wish for that world) to allow Himawari to be conceived... and so, Himawari fight to keep that world afloat?
Isn't that the worst time paradox ever?

Also, and I don't know why, but... «teen» Himawari (the one's oblivious about the reset) give me a strong Maya «vibe». And so, I still think she's tied to Maya in a extent... or Maya is the manifestation of a «perfect» daughter from Sensei perspective (which bring a lot more question about all the incest).

Finally, Himawari told us another thing : when they can't catch up someone during a «reset», that someone keep its memory... what did it imply? The rooftop isn't disallowed to them (Himawari was there at the end), so... what? There's another rooftop they can't go? Or no one really keep their memory?

Even if I can understand there's people who may want to end their life when an «apocalypse» appear (the reset kinda look like it), it will always feel strange to me...
The massacre in the dorm 4 for example was... strange. I understand why it would happen (given the state Futaba was), but still... Rin decapitated, Otoha over the couch... what kind of battle happen there?

Anyway, that's just me rambling... I'm not really here to search for an answer (my brain couldn't conceive them anyway), but visual novel like this permit me to grasp some understanding about people. Books too. Which is kinda sad, by the way.

Anyway, kinda surprised by that update. Didn't think it would be that story driven (I though it would just be about Ayane in another world...), so, yeah, I'm happy about it. And I'm happy that there's some answers (and some evolution for Sensei!), but... the chapter 4 isn't finished yet. The harem still need to be completed before we pass in chapter 5, so... my expectation go way down.

Still, I'm happy. Even if it make the world seem more and more off... at least, to me.

Full Spoilers and Massive amounts of tin foil:

So is "Our Akira" Akira 1, 2, or >3?

Akira 1 is ostensibly OG "Real World". People who live in the worlds who are not specifically created by the wish seem to be considered "Real People" along with the inhabitants of the OG world. OG world people seem to have a "higher status" then the "normal people" of all the other worlds given how Himawari speaks about them. Regardless, the wish world generated people seem to count as "real" in that wishes can be granted.

Since we now have hard evidence the Himawari is a real flesh and blood daughter, doesn't her definition of who's "normal people" mean that she can come from a world created by a wish?

If she originates from a wish world, wouldn't that make her existence as a "real person" (whose own wish is also demonstrably shown to work without any surprise) be true no matter how far down the rabbit hole she comes from?

With that in mind, the world really IS breaking because of Maya. "Our Maya" is Maya 2 from World 3 (Our current broken world).

Maya 1 was created as a Wish by World 1 "OG" Akira, which brings with it by default a new world (World 2). Everyone outside of Maya 1 is considered a "real Person" whose wish can be granted. Maya 1's Akira commits suicide, and she wished for the repeating Freshman year world the game is set in. Our World, World 3.

This should not be possible, given Maya 1 is a wish given form and not a "Real Person". However, since Maya 1's love/wish was so strong it somehow worked breaking the laws of reality. This is what gives the world its unstable nature.

Maya Prime (Maya 2) building belief of Sensei being the ACTUAL Sensei throughout Act 1 pushes her mind to the breaking point. She's insanely hopeful/certain that it really is him after receiving the scarf, but also immediately calls herself "the unluckiest girl in the world".

I think she always knew exactly why she was the unluckiest girl in the world.

Prime Maya (Maya 2) knew it was a wish world. She lied to us the whole time to a greater extent then we thought. Parallel timeline Maya admitted to experimenting with girls and various relationships in the parallel timeline whereas our Maya said differently. Parallel Maya also pointed out a handful of Prime Maya's other half-truths/lies. Everything deeply related to the nature of the world that was learned from Prime Maya has to be looked at with doubt in mind.

She knew that her Sensei's were always going to be imitations with varying imperfections. It seems whatever went wrong in Himawari's timeline caused Sensei's "soul" to "become available" and by pure chance manifested in the the Prime Maya wish world.

She finally got what she truly wished for, her real Akira. He now existed in her personal infinite world. She had only known for millions of years nothing but disappointment "fake" Akira's. Her codependency and jealousy skyrockets.

We see this essentially in most everything she does and says, always half truths and withholding information that parallel Maya freely passes with. Prime Maya and Parallel Maya both readily admit to being capable of sociopathic decisions/sacrifices, what's a lie here and there to them?

Prime Maya's (Maya 2) story of Vega and Altair is just a less sad version of her existence. At least Altair and Vega got to see each other once a year. Prime Maya (Maya 2) had literally zero hope/interactions with the "Real" Akira save for her memories of (ostensibly) Akira 2 that came from Maya 1's world.

But this is where I reach an impasse.

Both Prime Maya and Himawari seem to claim "Our Akira" as the "real" one to them. Prime Maya's "real" Akira would have to be the same as OG Maya's Akira right? That would infer our Akira is Akira 2. However, if that's true, how does Aoyama timeline exist? Himawari claims in no uncertain terms to be the real flesh and blood daughter of "Our Akira". But wouldn't that be Akira 2 as well?

How can we be both the Akira that leaves with Ayane, and the Akira that commits suicide in Maya 1's world?

IDK brain fried from banger update.


Side Note
I've read a lot of criticism of the writing here, not all unwarranted, for Chapter 4. We get indecisive Akira being sadder and more apathetic then ever, and you can certainly feel the "pause" in the plot progression.

But being able to play through a lot of those seemingly irrelevant and/or plodding events in 1 go instead of waiting each month for the next update gave me an entirely different impression, as I started with .51 and was lucky to skip the waiting.

I can absolutely see them as "frivolous" if I read Chapter 4 in more drip feed fashion. That gets really frustrating after a while, as anyone who was apart of the JJK leaks during peak 236 days can tell ya.

After 2 playthroughs, I think updates like this one give all the benefit of the doubt thats needed. So what if the lore gets a little squirrely. So what if it seems slow. If it gives us more character moments like this update I'm all for it.

This update hit like a ton of bricks. It gave tremendous plot progression and some of the saddest scenes (Himawari resets Akira and Ayane) in compensation for some of the happiest (Entirety of first part of the update).

This is easily a top 3 event chain in the game no matter how you look at it, its self evident.

All and all this was an absolute banger. From character moments to plot progression, I cant think of a more deeply relevent update.

She finally got what she truly wished for, her real Akira.  He now existed in her personal infinite world. She had only known for millions of years nothing but disappointment "fake" Akira's.  Her codependency and jealousy skyrockets.
We see this essentially in most everything she does and says, always half truths and withholding information that parallel Maya freely passes with.  Prime Maya and Parallel Maya both readily admit to being capable of sociopathic decisions/sacrifices, what's a lie here and there to them?
Prime Maya's (Maya 2) story of Vega and Altair is just a less sad version of her existence.  At least Altair and Vega got to see each other once a year.  Prime Maya (Maya 2) had literally zero hope/interactions with the "Real" Akira save for her memories of (ostensibly) Akira 2 that came from Maya 1's world.
But this is where I reach an impasse.
Both Prime Maya and Himawari seem to claim "Our Akira" as the "real" one to them.  Prime Maya's "real" Akira would have to be the same as OG Maya's Akira right?  That would infer our Akira is Akira 2.  However, if that's true, how does Aoyama timeline exist?  Himawari claims in no uncertain terms to be the real flesh and blood daughter of "Our Akira".  But wouldn't that be Akira 2 as well?
How can we be both the Akira that leaves with Ayane, and the Akira that commits suicide in Maya 1's world?
IDK brain fried from banger update.
Side Note
I've read a lot of criticism of the writing here, not all unwarranted, for Chapter 4.  We get indecisive Akira being sadder and more apathetic then ever, and you can certainly feel the "pause" in the plot progression.
But being able to play through a lot of those seemingly irrelevant and/or plodding events in 1 go instead of waiting each month for the next update gave me an entirely different impression, as I started with .51 and was lucky to skip the waiting.
I can absolutely see them as "frivolous" if I read Chapter 4 in more drip feed fashion.  That gets really frustrating after a while, as anyone who was apart of the JJK leaks during peak 236 days can tell ya.
After 2 playthroughs, I think updates like this one give all the benefit of the doubt thats needed.  So what if the lore gets a little squirrely.  So what if it seems slow.  If it gives us more character moments like this update I'm all for it.
This update hit like a ton of bricks.  It gave tremendous plot progression and some of the saddest scenes (Himawari resets Akira and Ayane) in compensation for some of the happiest (Entirety of first part of the update).
This is easily a top 3 event chain in the game no matter how you look at it, its self evident.
All and all this was an absolute banger.  From character moments to plot progression, I cant think of a more deeply relevent update.

posts.content_html_raw:
It was a good update. There are a lot of new lore and a lot of new questions.

There are so much Ayane shilling and Ami hating in this thread, I'm really confused. In my opinion, Ayane
is not good at all. Yeah, yeah, she likes her daughter, and she's romantic. And nothing else. She's doing nothing. She's simple, boring, vanilla, like a "normal ending" in any typical VN. She's not helping Akira in any way, she is simply existing. Like a tool to show us: see, you can live happily with her! Yay! Applause! Eww...

Himawari's
corporation also aren't "good guys". Even Himawari is blatanly lying to Akira and manipulating him (hiding stuff, telling that all is ok, which is an obvious lie). Maybe it's for a greater good, but she's very suspicious. I don't trust her "happiness" at all.


Unlike Ayane,
Ami is proactive: she's protecting her dad from troubles. Cause Maya is not real and also a source of these troubles, Ami sometimes is quite cold to her. She's also commiting suicide many times and fighting against huge celestial corporation for his and her own sake. Ayane is a weakling, but Ami is much stronger than her. She's a true hero, who don't afraid of some dirty work. And that's why she's the best girl in my eyes.

If we're doing some analogies,
Ayane is like Tomoe Mami, who lives happily and oblivious to the true nature of magical girls, who will immediately break in the moment she know the truth. Ami is like Akemi Homura, who is trying to save her beloved during hardships, failing and trying more and more, through pain and tears.

posts.content_html_raw:
Himawari saying "every day I grow some more" caused me to look back at the very first event of the entire game, titled the same.

Having spent the time following Himawari's description of where this universe came from, I couldn't help but notice that the narrator in the first event was sending the PoV character off to "someplace very special", this someplace special of course being the world-wished-by-Maya that we spend most of our in-game time in.

From Maya's (and Ami's) perspective, real Akira one day, after literally uncountable, untold numbers of timeloops, just showed up.

But putting it all together I realized something- real Akira only showed up because someone sent him there. Do we have any perspectives on who narrator from event one might be? Or might have been this whole time?

One weirdly troublesome part to me was how Himawari and Sensei essentially just ditched an absolutely shattered and mid-meltdown Ayane for a little bit there to do an impromptu "bring your father to work day". It tracks with what Ayane has had to roll with in the past and I get that the chapter was already very, very long without having to take time for such things, and clearly based on how all the characters treated it after they met back up implied that it isn't supposed to be that big a deal - but it still struck me as kind of fuckin' cold in spite of all that. Feels like people having meltdowns shouldn't be left alone. Still - a minor gripe in the face of the rest.

There's also the idea that Akira's extremely complicated, pervasive and often overwhelming traumas, insecurities and self-doubt can all be somewhat significantly healed by just ....having a child. I do get that 1) it's Himawari's wish-world so people's emotional states will be affected by the desires of the wishmaker and 2) Akira's a very special case in very special circumstances so there's room to argue and believe that having a child is a thing that could work on him in particular. But it still seems worth saying that this isn't how it's gonna usually work in real life, and the view that having a kid will fix someone usually just results in more childhood trauma.

Either way - this update was truly moving. This VN has moved me many, many times, in many, many ways, but not quite to this immense degree. The emotions were so genuinely expressed. There can only be exquisite beauty with some strangeness, indeed. I cried a lot - far more than I expected to even given the scenario - and I have to say at this point my emotional buy-in is pretty complete. It was before, but my coffin has now been well and truly nailed.

Wow... where do I even begin? That two month wait we had was definitely a tough one, but the update made up for it and then some. Sel knocked it out of the fucking park...

This update was by far my favorite showing of both Akira and Ayane both out of any other update of this game so far. To see a future with them as parents and how they interacted with Himawari was just incredible.

It's cathartic, really... seeing Akira care so much about Himawari after failing so hard with Ami. He's someone we've seen spend the entire game caring for little beyond himself; someone we've seen take a small step forward, then take five steps backwards again. It got to the point where it was hard to root for the guy, although I still maintained hope.

I felt warm inside. The entire update I did. I felt good. I felt intrigued as I watched how everything played out.

But I know this game by now. I braced for the inevitable impact...

Bam. Himawari zaps Akira and Ayane's memories of all their time together. Of what we just witnessed throughout the majority of the update.

Talk about fucking tragic...

Still... maybe there's hope. Akira and Ayane were having some deja vu at Christmalloween, so... fingers crossed they can regain those memories.

Oh yeah, then there was that threat from Ami at the end... I dunno man. I understand less about her more and more as each update goes by at this point. I'm just gonna wait until we get some more info on her.

My hope is that Akira can take what he learned in those months he was with Himawari to actually be a better father to Ami a little bit. At minimum, to maybe help her become less batshit insane?

Do I expect this to happen? Unlikely. Do I hope so? Of course.

I do like Ami from a character standpoint, even if I do miss our cute and wholesome niece from Chapter 1 sometimes. The next step (or one of them anyway) is surely finding out wtf her deal is and what god she's involved with. Not to mention the whole Maya thing.

I'm definitely excited for what's to come! Let's hope Sel can keep the ball rolling going into the next one.

I've also been wanting to do a new playthrough since my goals with saves and screenshots changed and trying to salvage them would be slower than just replaying the game again. That she loves that he's here, that we're here because she's been very very lonely. That she thinks we'll come to despise her in time. That this is her job, that she was chosen to be his mysterious anonymous narrator, that she wants to meet for real. That she knows this world was made for him and him alone, but that she can't tell you who made it nor why. And that if 'we' close our eyes she'll be there annoying us every step of the way.

I'm gonna try document screenshots in a useful way this time, basically have a save for every event and see if I can keep tags on every little piece of lore that appears. RIP my old 3324 screenshots you were made so I'd learn how annoyed I'd get screenshotting a quicksave label and clean it up properly this time.

I told myself I wasn't gonna throw my hat into the ring of theorycrafting but fuck it

The way I see it, who's defined as real and not is depending on regular worlds not made out of wishes. If you are capable of existing on any real world without the influence of a wish of any kind, that means you count as real person. That would make Maya the only anomaly, someone not capable of existing without a wish in non wish worlds and so Himawari isn't scrutinized for being an anomaly while Maya is

Note: This is my first theorycrafting on a game this complex so it's likely based on flimsy logic that could be disproven easily lmao

I believe Maya wished for a world where everyone loves Akira, where he doesn't have to feel threatened or scared by the people around him, and where he doesn't have to think about all of his trauma and damage anymore, and that she can be there and for that to be it, forever.

And if I were a betting person (I am not) I would bet that Maya phrased/thought about her wish like that or similar to that. That the wish was made in a moment of tremendous grief or emotion, she focused her wish on just taking his pain away and giving him what she thinks he wants - and she failed to actually say "I wish for a world where Akira is happy". Maybe because she wasn't thinking clearly, or as a selfish/self-preservation thing she actively didn't phrase it that way because maybe she knows a world where Akira is happy is a world that she's not in. She certainly didn't have a place in Ayane's epilogue, after all. She also didn't wish "a world where Akira and I can be together" because that's a given to her as long as the two of them exist - she believes that so fervently because HE wished for HER, after all.

Either way, I'd think it was as well-meaning a wish as a wished-person with a strange origin and stranger priorities could have.

posts.content_html_raw:
Not directly relevant to any other convo here:

It's incredible how instantly the use of "All That's Left Are Stars" communicated what kind of moment that was.

LiL is an experience that, inevitably, includes a lot of dread, a lot of unexpected terrors and emotionally disorienting whiplash and we're used to emotional rugpull moments being brain-shattering and shocking, to a degree. But this wasn't that- it was sad yes, heartbreaking absolutely, but the literal moment the pixellated visuals popped and the song started I was like "...oh. Yeah. Of course it was going to go this way.". And I really did believe for a good while there that it wasn't going to, too.

I'm glad Sel is good at using music to lend clarity and intensity to powerful emotional moments, because it's extremely effective.
