r_naxo0 said:
Most of the story is pointless now that Akira lost his memories after finally becoming happy.
Click to expand...
I think it's either that some people are missing a few details, or I'm the one with an issue. Let's recap a couple of things:
Himawari said all the way back in chapter 3 that she was "everything he never wanted, but all he'd ever need." That's the one answer about his happiness, it was never a question for her, she knows how he becomes happy, and now so do we.
What we saw during this update was the truth of that statement. Eventually, Akira and Ayane do have a child, and her presence grants Akira true hapiness. This is not a possibility, it's just factual. How exactly they arrive at that point is up in the air, but it does happen.

Himawari then joins the company to try to create the purity routes (which we know also happens, since it's where the game is moving towards), and to try to either prevent her parents from suffering so much, or to try to save them in the future while also ensuring that her meddling doesn't write her off of existence. Remember this last part, it's really important.

One point that is repeated across 0.53 is that Akira didn't deserve that ending. What we saw in Ayane's epilogue was a proof of concept. Selebus showed everyone that Akira will be healed, and that he will be happy, and that he will be able to stand up for his daughter and be an actual good person for her. He will have to run away from temptation, he will have to isolate himself from any mention of his past, he will have to cut ties with people that he thinks he loves and be unfair to them - which is quite realistic because he's way too broken for it to be pain-free, but he will do it. You can see how much Himawari worries about him being alone, he'll never be "safe", but he will try his best to not be a victim either. And that's an amazing ending.

BUT he needs to get there himself. An Akira that would have carried the memories of the end would just be unable to actually get there in a way that would result in that ending, or maybe even Himawari. And that's the danger and why she has to remove their memories of her. They need to continue living their lives and learning and hurting and growing until they get there.

The result of keeping those memories would be exactly what you said, they'd be half moping about it and half just laser-focused on getting back to Himawari, to the point where they'd draw attention to themselves and actively ignoring everyone else. Neither of those would lead to Himawari or a better ending than the one that she already got.

Thus, Ayane's epilogue is for Akira and Ayane and this amazing character that we have to say goodbye to (for now), but it is mostly for you and I. Because after years of Akira being passive and having reveals that just make it seem impossible for him to ever recover from the level of trauma he was put through, WE KNOW he will, we were shown that ending, and we lived that ending. And we all loved and cried with that ending.

So all the silly stuff and all the horrible stuff we'll see from now on is not balanced against a flimsy hope of "maybe things can get a little less awful", it is a tangible promise of going back to an even better version of our promised epilogue. It's not a "will he?", it's a "when will he?" and "will this help?" and "I hope he can save her too!" and "maybe her as well" and "how about all of them?"

0.53 is a gift to us, the players, in the form of making us all Himawari. She'll watch through her phone without being able to interfere anymore, but knowing that Akira can do it. And from hereafter we also know that he can do it. And that he will do it. And, hell, I love Himawari - and that's exactly why I think he ought to grant her her full dream.

Akira Arakawa will not only make it back to his daughter, he'll also save 35 girls, including the one that exists just for him. That's the game that begins now. After years and years, we've finally landed on solid ground. Himawari didn't remove the memories about either Maya or Ami, or the truth of this world, just about her - and we know that those will come back eventually as well. Ayane knew her name instantly upon seeing her, after all.
The game's looking better than it has for a LONG TIME.

Himawari then joins the company to try to create the purity routes (which we know also happens, since it's where the game is moving towards), and to try to either prevent her parents from suffering so much, or to try to save them in the future while also ensuring that her meddling doesn't write her off of existence. Remember this last part, it's really important.

One point that is repeated across 0.53 is that Akira didn't deserve that ending. What we saw in Ayane's epilogue was a proof of concept. Selebus showed everyone that Akira will be healed, and that he will be happy, and that he will be able to stand up for his daughter and be an actual good person for her. He will have to run away from temptation, he will have to isolate himself from any mention of his past, he will have to cut ties with people that he thinks he loves and be unfair to them - which is quite realistic because he's way too broken for it to be pain-free, but he will do it. You can see how much Himawari worries about him being alone, he'll never be "safe", but he will try his best to not be a victim either. And that's an amazing ending.

An Akira that would have carried the memories of the end would just be unable to actually get there in a way that would result in that ending, or maybe even Himawari. After years and years, we've finally landed on solid ground. Himawari didn't remove the memories about either Maya or Ami, or the truth of this world, just about her - and we know that those will come back eventually as well. Ayane knew her name instantly upon seeing her, after all.

Addressing some of your other questions as well, but focusing on this one because it's the easiest to explain.

Maya wished for a world where she could repeat that perfect moment in time with Akira, creating a time-loop bubble. That time loop bubble was a copy/paste of the original world, much like the quoted text above is a copy/paste from your original post.

Note how I only copy/pasted a part of your question. Everything else is gone. Does this make the quote I did copy fake? No, it's a copy, but just as "real" as your whole post.

That's what our Kumon Mi is. A copy/paste of the original world. The world is "fake" in a sense, but the people inside it are as real as their originals, though they are likely began drifting away from their "source code" almost as soon as they were created, as they are shaped by different experiences than their originals.

Makoto's father was outside the boundary when the copy/paste was done. He was never a part of our Kumon Mi, he only ever existed as a memory for those in Kumon Mi who remembered him from prior to the copy/paste wish. Since the original world was subject to linear time instead of the time loop, he's been dead for a very, very long time, as has everyone else who lived outside the bubble. Everything else is gone.

The Gods are watching Kumon Mi, because it shouldn't exist. It's an anomaly. It's entertainment. One of the Gods thought it would be funny to call Maki and inform her that her husband was dead just to see how far this anomaly can be pushed. That same God also thought it would be funny to call Haruka and inform her that her husband was still alive, just to see how far this anomaly can be pushed.

All the other instances of divine fuckery we see (Nozomu/HOPE pushing Akira do do X by Y time or Z happens) is also all likely just the Gods prodding the anomaly to see what happens. Maya's wish created a fishbowl, and they're just tapping the glass.

okokok said:
Why do Shiori and Himawari let Maya Prime exist for so long without meddling?
Click to expand...
I think that's a matter of perspective, in multiple fronts.
For one, "so long" matters little since we're talking about thousands of years. Maybe they have erased her a bunch of times before shifting to "just let her continue forever and see if that changes anything".

Other than that, there's also the thing about dodging them, are we absolutely sure that she did? Because Maya has a lot of missing memories. They say Ami is a menace because no matter what they erase, it comes back to her eventually, and they can't really exterminate her because even their most powerful employees (the peerless ones) will not touch her. That also means that they could erase/modify Maya's memories, since it's just Ami that's the outlier.

Another evidence is that Maya has been "alone" for how many resets? And yet she has not found ONE interaction between a custodian and a person, even though we know that it's super common for them to be walking around during the resets, and Ami is actively playing guerrilla wars against the custodians every cycle? But Maya has never encountered any of them interacting? That seems deliberate to me. Cause she does mention seeing other people that just "disappear" once "she resets the world", when we know that for someone to "disappear" there needs to be a custodian in the first place.

After all, it's not like no one can see eachother. The two Futabas and Rin suicide together. Ami activelly kills Nodoka, Yuki, Tsukasa and Tsubasa. They can see eachother no problem, and that's just for one reset. Imagine thousands of them. Himawari admits to having talked to Ami a whole bunch of times, and likely Nodoka as well.

Even if Maya truly has never encountered anyone else, and her memories aren't tampered with, that would mean it was under a directive not to mess with her, rather than her doing, I think. But, personally, I think it's more likely that her memory has been tampered with as well - since we have the events of Alternate Maya Prime and even the Scary Room. Moreover, the whole point of this world seems to be investigating her (and Akira because of her), so it'd make no sense for them not to experiment.
Unrelated to this, but I want to see a spin-off event of just being a custodian in one of those worlds now everyone's losing their minds over the reset and you're going around like "dude, I just work here".

posts.content_html_raw:
Hey everyone, how have you been? It's been a long time since my last comment. Life, trying to be a functional adult and a good dad, doesn't leave much time, but I've kept playing with every new update and reading the thread. Reading your analyses, opinions, and theories always helps me better organize my own thoughts and theories.
And what can I say about this latest update that hasn't already been said? I think this is the new peak for LiL. I doubt it's the absolute best Selebus can achieve, but it will take a while to surpass it. It's even funny that not too long ago we were at its lowest point (Fan Fest and Dorm Wars), but every update after that got better and better until reaching this point.
Ayane is undoubtedly the "best girl." She was already an S-Tier character for me, but now she's in her own category with Nikki. Himawari also won me over in a way I didn't expect.
Finally, I wanted to especially highlight my boy Akira. Seeing him finally become the human being I knew he could be was almost cathartic, and it completely was when I saw him become the protagonist of his own story and take, even if just a little, control of his life. As the end of the update approached, it became harder to hold back the tears until it was impossible. It was that good.

posts.content_html_raw:
The existence of the Are You Happy Here Twitter is really boggling, after taking a thorough look through it.
  • The first post for the account is in 2018. But anything regarding LiL or NiB wasn't made available till, the next year with NiB in 2019 and LiL in 2020. It could be related to Grow Old. Then Die. but I have no clue when the teaser for that was released, since Sel has archived the post for it.
    [*]The first piece of evidence linking this account to Kyoko is in 2021. A year after LiL release.
    [*]First mention of Shiori
    [*]Gossamer is mentioned a full 3 years before her initial intro at the beginning of Chapter 4 and mentioned is shown in full about a year before her introduction.
    [*] Kyoko shows Halftone before were introduced to him in Chapter 4
    [*]Kyoko makes mention of Himawari
The Are You Happy Here account is Kyoko's diary/journal and she somehow predates NiB and LiL. She mentions time and time again schizophrenically, that The Upside Down House is a prison and that she is constantly being watched. Death doesn't exist and time moves differently.

In a hex encoded message it reveals what the purpose of the Upside-down House is.
Whether the Upside Down House was created by Kyoko is up for debate. But Sel comments on the post this letter is in. Which I guess, makes him canon to the LiL extended universe???????? But Kyoko's many mentions of Shiori is interesting because, it implies that Shiori was once trapped or resided in the Upside Down House and was somehow able to get out. And Shiori refers to Kyoko in the past tense when looking at Nodoka. So this implies that she's been out of there for a minute.

There's also some audio clips that link to Sound Cloud. One of them is a distorted version of 'Daisy Bell' (the Daisy Daisy song) the other is a bunch of garbled junk, that I immediately clicked off of, before I summoned a demon. But in the little bit I did hear, it sounded to similar to the black cube that was speaking to Chika in her TSS.

Just some interesting tidbits I'd thought to share.

I agree with Budoop about Ami visiting her mother's tree and also about the lack of a showdown (Ami's victims all have the same white eyes as doll Sana, whereas her corpse doesn't because she was awake). I have some questions of my own about this scene:
1. Is it possible there were two Amis?

The last time we saw Ami before the reset (when she delivered the box) she was wearing pajamas, but the Ami corpse has her normal outfit. Would she really stop to change after the reset started? Especially since she can feel them coming according to Himawari (and she may have deliberately caused this one anyway).

There's precedent for the possibility of a clone. There were two Futabas during this reset, and Himawari says that happens sometimes in this world. During the Karaoke booth reset, we saw two Amis (there's a second Ami in the background after the first one is murdered). Maybe this is a strategy she uses to escape the custodians, letting them mind wipe the wrong Ami.

2. How (and why) did Nodoka get to the manor?

Her last know location was at the beach, which implies she somehow managed to be conscious and walk there. Maybe she followed Ami. On the other hand, the last known location wasn't accurate for Rin and Futaba, and Nodoka's white eyes imply she wasn't conscious. So maybe she was already at the manor before the reset started. The last we saw her, she talked to Touka about the tree and said she wanted to visit it.

I guess a way of reconciling the two is that Ami brought an unconscious Nodoka with her to the manor - seems impossible, but she claimed to do the same with Maya during the last reset. But I don't see a motive for Ami to do that, and it would be way too coincidental with Nodoka's last conversation.

Also interesting: Shiori says Nodoka is dead, but there's no obvious cause of death. Unlike Ami's other victims, there's no blood anywhere on her.

3. How does Tsubasa manage to remember things?

In her conversation with Himawari, Tsubasa talked about multiple worlds and said she met another custodian decades ago, implying she also knows about the resets. I had assumed she had her own way to survive them, but that doesn't appear to be the case. She got cleaned by Shiori along with the other corpses at the manor, so she should be mind wiped. But meeting a custodian is a memory that obviously would be erased, so how has she managed to retain it for so long?

On the Ami thing, there are so many replies I won't link any of them - but I did read them all.
Okay so, what if, hear me out, there are two Amis at this reset (or maybe in all of them)?

I think it'd be so awesome that maybe it's too awesome for Selebus. Let's call them "Sneak Ami" and "Cover Ami". Sneak Ami is the one that does all the murders and escapes the mind wipe, and Cover Ami is the one that gets caught by the custodians or "kills herself" to escape them.

While this is tinfoil, there is some evidence. For one, how did Cover Ami get all the way up there on the tree without a ladder? Well, if she had the help of another person, or it wasn't a suicide, but a murder, then Sneak Ami could just have removed the ladder later.

There is also evidence that there could be two Amis because there were two Futabas, and this seems to be somewhat regular. Second thing is that they are wearing different outfits after all. The Ami that killed New Maya wasn't wearing the same outfit as Cover Ami.

But this theory extends to something else, well, what if Ami is really just that smart that the reason she always retains her memories is because the custodians never catch Sneak Ami? Because she uses Cover Ami as a decoy, so if she escapes, fine, perfect memory throughout the reset. And if she gets caught, it doesn't matter, eventually the memories come back because the actual Ami (Sneak Ami) escaped.

So while the custodians search for Cover Ami, either they fail to catch her and never search for Sneak Ami. Or they catch Cover Ami, and stop searching because they don't realise there's another one.
I don't really believe in this tbh, but since we're throwing theories out there...

She was just trying to get information and prevent Akira and Ayane from being reset, from what I can tell. And maybe she was responsible for Maya's eventual demise (not on purpose), but from her bootstrap scarf.

I don't think anyone has talked about this either, so let's talk about it.

Himawari seems to not have joined from the start, I don't think, otherwise she'd have likely been spotted by now - I think it's likely she started working there because of our Akira, which is hers as well. So, how Himawari intended to get more information that was unable to be acquired by the company over so long? My guess is that she tried investigating both Ami and Maya. The Ami part I'm unsure about because I don't have evidence about it for now, but we can safely assumed that she tried talking to her a couple of times and had Shiori torture her for info as well.

But, regarding Maya, my guess was that the whole thing had to do with the scarf. And since the scarf resulted in nothing as of this reset, my guess was that it was already used. For this to work, people have to understand what a "bootstrap paradox" is. This paradox happens when an object has no discernible point of origin, due to timetravel.

A Doctor Who example of this was that a timetraveler loved Beethoven's music, so they go back in the past to meet him. But when they arrive, no one has ever heard of him - and the timetraveler despairs at the idea of a world without his favorite composer. Thus, he calls himself Beethoven, and publishes all of his compositions as if he was Beethoven himself. When he goes back to the future, history is the same, and no one could have guessed that Beethoven was a timetraveler. But then, the question remains: who actually wrote the compositions in the first place? This is called bootstrap paradox.

Well, we have known for quite a while that the one that sells Akira the scarves is Himawari.
Maya breaks down upon receiving it because it is the actual scarf Akira gave her when she was young
This is the moment that Maya accepts Akira as her Akira. Akira says so himself, it was the first time she started following him. And all of this only happens because of direct Himawari manipulation, which we now know, is because she's trying to get some sort of information from this too. It's important to remember that Akira and Ayane manage to somehow escape and give birth to Himawari without any of this. Thus her reason for doing it is likely that she wants some sort of info that helps her own plans.

Okay, but, well, where did Himawari get it?
Well, she got it from Ayane, and most importantly, she didn't keep it. "It was show time" likely also means that the scarf was used, and more importantly, her giving it to someone was a huge part of the plan. Just to cover all bases, this one scarf was dragged here from Maya herself, meaning that this is the actual scarf Akira gave her when she was young (notice how Himawari says that is it old).
So, from this, we get that the actual plan to use the scarf to wake her up was from alt Maya Prime in the first place, but what I'm proposing is that Himawari took that scarf and gave to Maya Prime in the past, rather than New Maya.

Well, why all this theory thing instead of just assuming Himawari didn't do anything with the scarf? Like just preventing it from waking New Maya? Well, it's because she says so herself:
Himawari has been fined multiple times with bootstrapping. Which means that she has been adding future knowledge/objects into the past, thus creating paradoxes where those very future things become the past objects/knowledge that would give birth to them in the future.

Think about it, all that we're seeing since Maya received the scarf is because she got the scarf in the first place, leading her to trust Akira, accepting his feelings and displaying her own, until she got done by the end of chapter 3. That also means that Ayane wouldn't ever have met with alt Maya Prime to get the scarf in the first place, if Maya Prime hadn't received it from Akira/Himawari. Thus making it all a bootstrap paradox.

Furthermore, we know Himawari was deeply involved with Maya's "awakening"/acceptance of this Akira as hers.


also, get ready to cry right now:




Hilariousmawari. And she doesn't go to school because she's homeschooled by him.
She's also on the rooftoop during "glued to the sky" when Akira's talking to Maya after Niki confesses.

Well, all of this is to represent how she has invested interest in Maya and the repercussions of the scarf. She also knows Maya is going to get caught at the end of Chapter 3, which would be impossible to know if she was living alongside Akira in this timeline.
Now, the way I interpret this is that she's talking about Maya, and thus it validates the idea that she knows the future. But it could also be that she's talking about Ayane and so it justifies her saving her? Well, the feeling about the end of the chapter is definitely Maya though.

One last comment about timetravel being a thing, although not from Himawari, sort of validates it:
One aspect we didn't quite discuss is the people that were actively helped by Himawari were the ones on Ami's hitlist this time. Nodoka and Tsubasa to be exact:

Then we see both of them dead in the Tsukioka manor. The one logical connection between them would be Himawari after all. Although Nodoka, ultimately, went there through Touka - Himawari has been showing up in her dreams for a long time.
So Nodoka went there for Sekai's body, which seems to be the mystery of how Ami is untouchable - but that might be a leap. Not that much of a leap though. If Sekai wrote her last poem to Akira or Ami, it remains to be seen.

Regardless, one of the ways that I see the game moving towards is the mystery of Sekai becoming a god under the everblooming sakura, and Ami being one of the ways we get to understanding that, since she's clearly been protected by it/knows about it (since she went there when the world was literally ending).

The other is Maya and this being her world. At the end of the day, Himawari joined the company to create the purity routes and be able to achieve something her parents couldn't. That means she has to acquire information through messing with this world, so that it gives her answers it didn't give to her parents in their run.

Now that she's out, it's up to Akira and Ayane to extract that information from Ami (that actively has it) and Maya (that is the key to it, but doesn't have it). All the while, Nodoka, that was previously reset by Pareidolia, now has Shiori on her corner (our new main custodian for TERMINAL23) - so she may be able to offer even more help.
On a last note, unless otherwise disproven, I think that this last update reinforces the idea of how most of the gods are just white noise. Neither the Maya, Ami, Nodoka, or Himawari lines have anything to do with them exactly. Akira and Sekai's stories sort of do, but it's also more about the idea of gods in general, rather than a specific god, like we're told to assume from the first chapters.

HOPE, Wires are Pareidolia are barely a thing in my mind when I think about the game right now - and I think that's a good thing. I feel that for a long time the game has been drifting in its multitude of gods and now it feels more grounded. They all are shown taking a look at Himawari manipulating her parents memories at the end and it's just "well, whatever, who cares about these people" (the three moons seem to be HOPE, Wires and Pareidolia though, from their faces).
Anyway, it's been a long post with a lot of ideas, I hope some of them help or spark discussions of their own.

But, regarding Maya, my guess was that the whole thing had to do with the scarf. And since the scarf resulted in nothing as of this reset, my guess was that it was already used. For this to work, people have to understand what a "bootstrap paradox" is. This paradox happens when an object has no discernible point of origin, due to timetravel.
A Doctor Who example of this was that a timetraveler loved Beethoven's music, so they go back in the past to meet him. But when they arrive, no one has ever heard of him - and the timetraveler despairs at the idea of a world without his favorite composer. Thus, he calls himself Beethoven, and publishes all of his compositions as if he was Beethoven himself. When he goes back to the future, history is the same, and no one could have guessed that Beethoven was a timetraveler. But then, the question remains: who actually wrote the compositions in the first place? This is called bootstrap paradox.

spoilers.title: The future of the game
spoilers.html:
One aspect we didn't quite discuss is the people that were actively helped by Himawari were the ones on Ami's hitlist this time. Nodoka and Tsubasa to be exact:
View attachment 5410496 View attachment 5410501 View attachment 5410498

Then we see both of them dead in the Tsukioka manor. The one logical connection between them would be Himawari after all. Although Nodoka, ultimately, went there through Touka - Himawari has been showing up in her dreams for a long time.
View attachment 5410503 View attachment 5410504 View attachment 5410506 View attachment 5410507
So Nodoka went there for Sekai's body, which seems to be the mystery of how Ami is untouchable - but that might be a leap. Not that much of a leap though. If Sekai wrote her last poem to Akira or Ami, it remains to be seen.

Regardless, one of the ways that I see the game moving towards is the mystery of Sekai becoming a god under the everblooming sakura, and Ami being one of the ways we get to understanding that, since she's clearly been protected by it/knows about it (since she went there when the world was literally ending).

The other is Maya and this being her world. At the end of the day, Himawari joined the company to create the purity routes and be able to achieve something her parents couldn't. That means she has to acquire information through messing with this world, so that it gives her answers it didn't give to her parents in their run.

Now that she's out, it's up to Akira and Ayane to extract that information from Ami (that actively has it) and Maya (that is the key to it, but doesn't have it). All the while, Nodoka, that was previously reset by Pareidolia, now has Shiori on her corner (our new main custodian for TERMINAL23) - so she may be able to offer even more help.

spoilers.title: on gods
spoilers.html:
On a last note, unless otherwise disproven, I think that this last update reinforces the idea of how most of the gods are just white noise. Neither the Maya, Ami, Nodoka, or Himawari lines have anything to do with them exactly. Akira and Sekai's stories sort of do, but it's also more about the idea of gods in general, rather than a specific god, like we're told to assume from the first chapters.

HOPE, Wires are Pareidolia are barely a thing in my mind when I think about the game right now - and I think that's a good thing. I feel that for a long time the game has been drifting in its multitude of gods and now it feels more grounded. They all are shown taking a look at Himawari manipulating her parents memories at the end and it's just "well, whatever, who cares about these people" (the three moons seem to be HOPE, Wires and Pareidolia though, from their faces).
